331	extension Exporter {
332	
333	    /// Why an export stopped. Every case is reported through `completion` —
334	    /// nothing here throws at the caller and nothing crashes.
335	    enum ExportError: LocalizedError {
336	        /// The core could not produce a composition plan for this project.
337	        case noPlan
338	        /// Nothing to write: no video and no audio track in the plan. Reached
339	        /// by an empty timeline AND by one holding only text, shapes and
340	        /// images, which need no composition track (spec §7.2) — so the
341	        /// message has to name the second case, which is the surprising one.
342	        case emptyTimeline
343	        /// This Mac will not encode what the core's preset resolved to — an
344	        /// unknown codec name, one `AVAssetWriter` refuses an input for, or
345	        /// one whose encoder is not found when the write starts
346	        /// (`Exporter.encoderOutcome`). Carries the preset id when the core
347	        /// gave one, else the codec.
348	        case presetUnavailable(String)
349	        /// The settings named a container this build cannot map to a file
350	        /// type.
351	        case fileTypeUnsupported(String)
352	        /// An alpha-carrying row was asked for a size of a different SHAPE
353	        /// from the canvas, which cannot be written correctly and so is not
354	        /// written at all (road map 2, phase 7b). Carries the canvas and the
355	        /// size the core resolved, in that order.
356	        ///
357	        /// **Which sizes reach it** (spec §11 G-33 (c)): on `prores_4444` and
358	        /// `hevc_alpha`, a frame more than a pixel off the canvas's shape
359	        /// (`ExportWriter.shapeGap`: `gap > limit`). A frame within a pixel is
360	        /// filled instead of padded and is written — the evened Document row
361	        /// on a canvas with an odd edge, a standard row whose long edge
362	        /// rounded, a size typed in the canvas's own proportions (evened
363	        /// first on `hevc_alpha`, so an odd one is written a pixel smaller),
364	        /// and on `prores_4444` a typed frame one pixel short. So no size of
365	        /// the canvas's shape is refused for being odd; a typed size of any
366	        /// other shape is judged as the even frame it becomes
367	        /// (1279 × 720 on 1920 × 1080 is 1278 × 720 on `hevc_alpha`, and
368	        /// refused).
369	        ///
370	        /// **Measured, not feared.** `AVVideoScalingModeResizeAspect` pads
371	        /// the frame to the asked-for shape, and the padding path destroys
372	        /// the alpha channel: a 320 × 180 transparent canvas written
373	        /// `prores_4444` at 240 × 240 comes back with the PICTURE at alpha 0
374	        /// and the letterbox BARS at alpha 255 — the answer inverted, not
375	        /// merely lost. The same canvas at 160 × 90 or 640 × 360 is correct
376	        /// at every pixel, so the fault is the padding and nothing else.
377	        ///
378	        /// It is refused rather than documented because the file would be
379	        /// silently wrong in the one respect the row exists for, and this
380	        /// codebase's rule for exactly that shape is `codecType(for:)`'s:
381	        /// a refusal, never a fallback that puts a file on disk which is not
382	        /// the one asked for. Nothing legitimate is blocked by accident —
383	        /// every row of the Size popup is fitted to the document's own
384	        /// aspect (`export_size.rs`), so only a hand-typed Custom size of
385	        /// another shape can reach this (or a canvas, or a typed size, with
386	        /// an edge of exactly 1 px, raised to 2 on `hevc_alpha`), and the
387	        /// message says what to type instead: every size with the canvas's
388	        /// proportions is written, odd or even, smaller or larger.
389	        case alphaAspectMismatch(width: Int, height: Int, wantWidth: Int, wantHeight: Int)
390	        /// The user pressed Cancel. The sheet dismisses without an alert.
391	        case cancelled
392	        /// The write ended in a state that is neither completed nor
393	        /// cancelled and had no error of its own — or one of the reader's or
394	        /// writer's own steps refused with a message worth showing.
395	        case failed(String)
396	        /// Graphic clips in the range whose module does not compile, or is
397	        /// not in `graphics/`, each with what is wrong: the export was refused
398	        /// before it started (G-8). Sorted by name.
399	        case graphicsNotCompiled([(name: String, message: String)])

497	/// Pass one of an export: read the composed mix and MEASURE it (`Loudness.swift`).
498	///
499	/// This is `Exporter`'s own "Measuring the mix" section, in a file of its own
500	/// because `Exporter.swift` went past app/CLAUDE.md's ~600-line cap when phase
501	/// 5 put a second pass in it. It is a MOVE and nothing else — the same methods,
502	/// the same order, the same bodies — so `Exporter.swift`'s five internal members
503	/// (`lock`, `measuring`, `scratchStorage`, `scratchCapacity`, and the
504	/// `isCancelled` / `setMeasureProgress` accessors over that lock) are internal
505	/// only to be reachable from here. Stored properties cannot live in an
506	/// extension, which is the whole reason the split is where it is.
507	///
508	/// **What it buys.** Every export that carries sound gets a measured
509	/// "Peak −1.0 dBTP · −14.0 LUFS" on its final line, and an export that asked to
510	/// be normalised gets the gain that lands it on its target. The pass is a
511	/// reader with no writer, no video output and no encoder — audio decode through
512	/// the plan's own mix, and nothing else — so it costs a few per cent of a movie
513	/// export and roughly doubles an audio-only one, which is also the case where
514	/// the number matters most.
515	///
516	/// **It builds its OWN composition.** An `AVAudioMix` copy shares the
517	/// `MTAudioProcessingTap` objects its input parameters hold, and a tap carries
518	/// per-instance state (the compressor's envelope, the noise reducer's delay
519	/// line), so two readers over one mix would interleave into one tap's. Running
520	/// them strictly in sequence would *probably* survive on `AudioTapContext`'s
521	/// start-of-stream reset — but not for a range shorter than its 0.1 s seek
522	/// tolerance, and a second build costs one more pass of opening asset tracks on
523	/// a queue that exists for exactly that and removes the argument entirely. It is
524	/// the same movie by construction: the same plan JSON, the same media, the same
525	/// recipe slot. Its `videoComposition` is never read. `Exporter.export` is where
526	/// that second build happens; everything below is what it is handed.
527	///
528	/// **Nothing here can fail an export.** Every refusal is a nil, which means "no
529	/// loudness figure" and never "no file": the write pass that follows is the one
530	/// that decides whether there is one.
531	extension Exporter {
532	
533	    // MARK: - Measuring the mix
534	
535	    /// What the measurement READS: `ExportAudioMaster.floatMixSettings`, the
536	    /// one float dictionary, and the same one every export's write pass reads
537	    /// (spec §11 #86, AU-27). So the gain is applied to exactly the signal
538	    /// measured here, and the master limits it.
539	    ///
540	    /// **Why float.** Int16 SATURATES. A mix hotter than full scale — which
541	    /// is exactly the material loudness normalisation exists for — would be
542	    /// measured clipped, and its true peak would be pinned at 0 dBTP by the
543	    /// decode rather than by the signal. Read as float, the overshoot is
544	    /// measured whole and the master holds it at its ceiling.
545	    ///
546	    /// **Why the rate and the channel count are the writer's.** BS.1770-4
547	    /// sums weighted channel powers and left and right both carry 1.0, so
548	    /// the same signal measured as one channel and written as two is 3.01 LU
549	    /// apart. An `AVAssetReaderAudioMixOutput` will happily give one channel
550	    /// to a caller who asks; measuring at a shape the file is not written at
551	    /// is a silent 3 dB error.
552	    private static let measureSampleRate: Double = 48000
553	    private static let measureChannelCount = 2
554	    private static let measureAudioSettings = ExportAudioMaster.floatMixSettings
555	
556	    /// The same, in the writer's own 16-bit integer. Nothing in this tree had
557	    /// asked an `AVAssetReaderAudioMixOutput` for float before phase 5, so
558	    /// the float request is MEASURED with `canAdd` rather than assumed and
559	    /// this is what a refusal falls back to — a measurement of a signal
560	    /// clipped at full scale is still better than no measurement, and the
561	    /// fallback is recorded here rather than discovered as a wrong number.
562	    ///
563	    /// **Measured on macOS 26.5.1: the float request is accepted**
564	    /// (`canAdd` answered true over a composition with one audio track and a
565	    /// mix, and the pass measured EBU Tech 3341 case 1 at −22.994 LUFS
566	    /// against its −23.0). So this dictionary is insurance and not a path
567	    /// anything here has taken; if it ever is taken, the loudness of a mix
568	    /// with no headroom problem is unaffected and the true peak of one that
569	    /// has is pinned at 0 dBTP. A fallback read records no 10 ms steps, so
570	    /// the gain is then the unlimited one (spec §11 AU-28).
571	    private static let measureFallbackAudioSettings: [String: Any] = [
572	        AVFormatIDKey: Int(kAudioFormatLinearPCM),
573	        AVSampleRateKey: 48000,
574	        AVNumberOfChannelsKey: 2,
575	        AVLinearPCMBitDepthKey: 16,
576	        AVLinearPCMIsFloatKey: false,
577	        AVLinearPCMIsBigEndianKey: false,
578	        AVLinearPCMIsNonInterleaved: false,
579	    ]
580	
581	    /// Pass one: read the composed mix and measure it. `buildQueue`, never
582	    /// the main thread.
583	    ///
584	    /// The range is the SETTINGS' — `Exporter.timeRange`, the same one the
585	    /// writer will read — and not the composition's own duration, or the
586	    /// measurement would cover a different span than the file. No video
587	    /// output is added, which is the whole reason the pass is cheap. A float
588	    /// read also feeds `StepLoudnessMeter`, whose 10 ms steps the gain is
589	    /// solved over under the master (spec §11 AU-28).
590	    ///
591	    /// nil for a composition with no sound, for a read this Mac refuses, and
592	    /// for a cancel. A nil is "no loudness figure", never a failed export:
593	    /// the write that follows is the one that decides whether there is a
594	    /// file. A normalisation that was asked for and could not be measured
595	    /// therefore writes UN-normalised, and the missing line on the progress
596	    /// sheet is how that shows — which is honest for the only case that
597	    /// reaches it in practice (a timeline with no sound at all), because
598	    /// every other nil here is a decode failure the write pass runs into a
599	    /// moment later and reports as the error it is.
600	    func measureLoudness(
601	        _ built: BuiltComposition, settings: ExportSettings
602	    ) -> ExportLoudness? {
603	        let tracks = built.composition.tracks(withMediaType: .audio)
604	        guard !tracks.isEmpty, let reader = try? AVAssetReader(asset: built.composition),
605	            let meter = LoudnessMeter(
606	                sampleRate: Exporter.measureSampleRate,
607	                channelCount: Exporter.measureChannelCount)
608	        else { return nil }
609	        let stepMeter = StepLoudnessMeter()
610	        let range = Exporter.timeRange(settings, composition: built.composition)
611	        let seconds = max(0, CMTimeGetSeconds(range.duration))
612	        reader.timeRange = range
613	        // Only the frames the file will hold are measured (spec §11 #337).
614	        let limit = ExportAudioEnd.frames(ofTicks: CompositionBuilder.ticks(range.duration))
615	        var fed = 0
616	
617	        // A build whose tracks have dynamics is measured through their
618	        // sub-mixes (`ExportMixRead`, spec §11 AU-152), float only: there is
619	        // no 16-bit fallback for it.
620	        let mixRead = ExportMixRead(built, origin: range.start)
621	        let subMixed = mixRead.isSubMixed
622	        var isFloat = true
623	        var output = Exporter.mixOutput(tracks, mix: built.audioMix, float: true)
624	        if subMixed {
625	            guard mixRead.add(to: reader) else { return nil }
626	        } else {
627	            if !reader.canAdd(output) {
628	                isFloat = false
629	                output = Exporter.mixOutput(tracks, mix: built.audioMix, float: false)
630	                guard reader.canAdd(output) else { return nil }
631	            }
632	            reader.add(output)
633	        }
634	        guard reader.startReading() else { return nil }
635	        lock.lock()
636	        measuring = true
637	        lock.unlock()
638	        defer {
639	            lock.lock()
640	            measuring = false
641	            lock.unlock()
642	        }
643	
644	        let read = { () -> CMSampleBuffer? in
645	            subMixed ? (try? mixRead.next()) ?? nil : output.copyNextSampleBuffer()
646	        }
647	        while let sample = read() {
648	            guard !isCancelled else {
649	                reader.cancelReading()
650	                return nil
651	            }
652	            fed += feed(
653	                sample, to: meter, steps: isFloat ? stepMeter : nil, float: isFloat,
654	                limit: limit - fed)
655	            guard seconds > 0 else { continue }
656	            let elapsed = CMTimeGetSeconds(
657	                CMSampleBufferGetPresentationTimeStamp(sample) - range.start)
658	            setMeasureProgress(min(max(elapsed / seconds, 0), 1))
659	        }
660	        guard reader.status == .completed else { return nil }
661	        setMeasureProgress(1)
662	        let measuredSteps = isFloat ? stepMeter.finish() : (steps: [], peaks: [])
663	        return ExportLoudness.resolve(
664	            measured: meter.finish(), steps: measuredSteps.steps, peaks: measuredSteps.peaks,
665	            target: settings.loudnessLufs, ceiling: settings.masterCeilingDBTP)
666	    }
667	
668	    /// One read-only output over the plan's mix — the same taps, the same
669	    /// volume ramps the writer will read through.
670	    private static func mixOutput(
671	        _ tracks: [AVAssetTrack], mix: AVAudioMix?, float: Bool
672	    ) -> AVAssetReaderAudioMixOutput {
673	        let output = AVAssetReaderAudioMixOutput(
674	            audioTracks: tracks,
675	            audioSettings: float ? measureAudioSettings : measureFallbackAudioSettings)
676	        output.audioMix = mix
677	        // Nothing here writes a sample back, so there is no reason to pay
678	        // for a copy of every buffer (`MediaImporter.peaks` is the precedent).
679	        output.alwaysCopiesSampleData = false
680	        return output
681	    }
682	
683	    /// One sample buffer into the meter, and on a float read the step meter
684	    /// too, at most `limit` frames of it; the frames fed.
685	    ///
686	    /// A `CMBlockBuffer` may be several non-contiguous chunks, and
687	    /// `CMBlockBufferGetDataPointer` on the first one silently truncates the
688	    /// buffer — the trap `MediaImporter.peaks` records and
689	    /// `ReverseRenderer.appendAudioBytes` avoids the same way.
690	    private func feed(
691	        _ sample: CMSampleBuffer, to meter: LoudnessMeter, steps: StepLoudnessMeter?,
692	        float: Bool, limit: Int
693	    ) -> Int {
694	        guard limit > 0, let block = CMSampleBufferGetDataBuffer(sample) else { return 0 }
695	        let width = float ? MemoryLayout<Float>.size : MemoryLayout<Int16>.size
696	        let frames = min(
697	            CMBlockBufferGetDataLength(block) / (width * Exporter.measureChannelCount), limit)
698	        let byteCount = frames * width * Exporter.measureChannelCount
699	        guard frames > 0, let bytes = scratch(ofAtLeast: byteCount) else { return 0 }
700	        guard CMBlockBufferCopyDataBytes(
701	            block, atOffset: 0, dataLength: byteCount, destination: bytes)
702	            == kCMBlockBufferNoErr
703	        else { return 0 }
704	        if float {
705	            let floats = bytes.bindMemory(to: Float.self, capacity: byteCount / width)
706	            meter.feed(floats, frames: frames)
707	            steps?.feed(floats, frames: frames)
708	        } else {
709	            meter.feedInt16(
710	                bytes.bindMemory(to: Int16.self, capacity: byteCount / width), frames: frames)
711	        }
712	        return frames
713	    }
714	
715	    private func scratch(ofAtLeast bytes: Int) -> UnsafeMutableRawPointer? {
716	        if scratchCapacity < bytes {
717	            scratchStorage?.deallocate()
718	            scratchStorage = .allocate(byteCount: bytes, alignment: 16)
719	            scratchCapacity = bytes
720	        }
721	        return scratchStorage
722	    }

726	/// An audio export's stems (spec §11 AU-108): the mix, then one file per stem

906	        lock.lock()
907	        current = writer
908	        let cancelled = cancelRequested
909	        lock.unlock()
910	        if cancelled { writer.cancel() }
911	        writer.start { [weak self] result in self?.ended(result, at: url, next: index + 1) }
912	    }
913	
914	    /// Removes every file this job wrote, then reports `error`.
915	    private func fail(_ error: any Error) {
916	        for url in written { try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: url) }
917	        written = []
918	        complete(.failure(error))
919	    }
920	
921	    private func complete(_ result: Result<URL, any Error>) {
922	        let handler = completion
923	        completion = nil
924	        handler?(result)
925	    }
926	}

3	/// What the export sheet's controls MEAN, before any of them has been read:
4	/// the ranges the fields accept, the loudness targets and the fixed ceiling,
5	/// the quality ladder and its arithmetic, and `Applies` — the one reading of
6	/// a format that decides which of the sheet's controls that row can honestly
7	/// take.
8	///
9	/// The seam is between a control's VOCABULARY and its VALUE.
10	/// `ExportSheetController.swift` builds the popups and the fields and puts
11	/// the card up; `ExportSheetResolve.swift` reads what is chosen and asks the
12	/// core about it. Everything here is what both of them consult and neither
13	/// of them owns: it depends on no popup's selection, holds no state, and
14	/// would answer the same for a sheet that was never shown. That is also why
15	/// the two nested types live in this half rather than beside the controls
16	/// they gate — `QualityTier` is a bit-rate calculation and `Applies` is a
17	/// reading of one `ExportPreset` row, and neither has ever asked an
18	/// `NSPopUpButton` a question.

20	/// The cut is the size payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed at 1114
21	/// lines against app/CLAUDE.md's ~600 cap, and it is a pure move: the same
22	/// declarations, in the same order, with the same bodies. **The toll is
23	/// visibility.** `private` on an extension member reaches only its own file,
24	/// so `loudnessTargets`, `loudnessRange`, `tiers`, `QualityTier`, `Applies`,
25	/// `isFrameSequence` and `rateText` are all internal now, for the reason
26	/// `ExporterLoudness.swift` records: the split, and nothing else. `sizeRange`
27	/// and `peakCeilingDBTP` were already internal and say in their own comments
28	/// why. `loudnessTitle` arrived later, in phase 7, and for the other reason a
29	/// member moves: the controller was at the cap and had to give something up
30	/// before it took the Preset row on.
31	extension ExportSheetController {

33	    /// The widest and narrowest custom size the fields accept. Not a format
34	    /// limit: a sanity range so a mistyped digit cannot ask the encoder for a
35	    /// 300 000-pixel frame.
36	    /// Internal, not private: the agent's `export` refuses a custom size
37	    /// outside it by name (`AgentServer+Export.swift`), and one constant is
38	    /// how the sheet and the tool cannot disagree.
39	    static let sizeRange = 16...8192

41	    // MARK: - Loudness
42	
43	    /// The Loudness popup's rows after "Off", in menu order: the integrated
44	    /// target each asks the export to be normalised to.
45	    ///
46	    /// −14 LUFS is where every streaming service has settled (Spotify,
47	    /// YouTube and Apple Music all normalise to within a decibel of it), −16
48	    /// is the podcast convention for stereo, and −23 is EBU R 128, which is
49	    /// broadcast delivery in Europe and what "LUFS" meant before streaming
50	    /// took the word. Anything else is "Custom…" and the field beside it.
51	    static let loudnessTargets: [Double] = [-14, -16, -23]
52	
53	    /// The true-peak ceiling of the master limiter every export with sound
54	    /// runs (spec §11 AU-27), in dBTP, sent only beside a loudness target —
55	    /// unsent, the master holds the same −1 (`ExportLoudness.defaultCeiling`).
56	    /// FIXED in phase 5 rather than made a control: five presets and
57	    /// one broadcast-standard ceiling is what people actually pick, the sheet
58	    /// is already six control rows deep, and the `export` tool keeps
59	    /// `peak_dbtp` for a script that needs −0.3 or −2.0. The hint says the
60	    /// number, so a fixed value is visible rather than folklore.
61	    static let peakCeilingDBTP: Double = -1
62	
63	    /// A target as its menu row reads. The two named tiers say who asks for
64	    /// them, because "−14" and "−23" mean nothing to someone who has not met
65	    /// them before and everything to someone who has.
66	    ///
67	    /// Here rather than beside the popup it titles, and the move is the size
68	    /// payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed before phase 7 put a Preset
69	    /// row and a burn-in on it. It belongs in this half by this file's own
70	    /// rule: it is a pure function of a target, holds no state, asks no
71	    /// control anything, and is `rateText`'s sibling — the spelling of one of
72	    /// the ladders `loudnessTargets` and `tiers` declare a few lines up.
73	    static func loudnessTitle(_ target: Double) -> String {
74	        let value = String(format: "%.0f", target).replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−")
75	        switch target {
76	        case -14: return "\(value) LUFS (streaming)"
77	        case -23: return "\(value) LUFS (broadcast)"
78	        default: return "\(value) LUFS"
79	        }
80	    }

82	    /// What the core will take: `export_overrides.rs`'s own bounds for
83	    /// `loudness_lufs`, spelled here so the field's formatter refuses what
84	    /// the core would refuse rather than sending it and reading the message

88	    // MARK: - Quality
89	
90	    /// One row of the Quality popup: a video rate expressed as bits per pixel
91	    /// per frame, and the AAC rate that goes with it.
92	    ///
93	    /// **Where the video numbers come from.** They are anchored on one
94	    /// published figure and scaled from it rather than guessed: YouTube's
95	    /// recommended upload for 1080p SDR H.264 at 30 fps is 8 Mbps, and
96	    /// 1920 × 1080 × 30 is 62.2 Mpixel/s, so "High" is 8 000 000 / 62 200 000
97	    /// ≈ 0.129 bits per pixel per frame. The other three tiers are 0.5×,
98	    /// 0.75× and 1.5× of it — 4, 6 and 12 Mbps at 1080p30, which brackets
99	    /// Apple's HLS Authoring Specification 1080p H.264 rung (6.0–7.8 Mbps)
100	    /// on both sides.
101	    ///
102	    /// Holding bits-per-pixel constant makes the rate scale with the frame's
103	    /// area, so High is 3.6 Mbps at 720p and 32 Mbps at 4K. That is
104	    /// deliberately flatter than YouTube's own ladder, which is generous at
105	    /// the small end because its rungs are transcode targets; a master at a
106	    /// constant bits-per-pixel is the same picture at every size, which is
107	    /// what choosing "High" ought to mean.
108	    struct QualityTier {
109	        let name: String
110	        /// Bits per pixel per frame, for H.264 at 30 fps or less.
111	        let bitsPerPixel: Double
112	        /// AAC-LC stereo, bits per second. 128 kbps is the streaming
113	        /// baseline, 256 is what Apple Music ships, and 320 is where AAC-LC
114	        /// stops paying for the extra bits.
115	        let audioBitsPerSecond: Int
116	
117	        /// The video rate for a `width` × `height` frame at `fps`.
118	        ///
119	        /// The 30 is not a stand-in for `fps`: the frame rate enters through
120	        /// `rateFactor` instead, because bits do not scale linearly with it.
121	        /// Consecutive frames are more alike the closer together they are,
122	        /// which is why YouTube's ladder asks 1.5× for its 48–60 fps column
123	        /// and nothing extra for 24 fps over 30. This mirrors that shape —
124	        /// one step at 30 and below, one above it.
125	        func videoBitsPerSecond(width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps, codec: String) -> Int {
126	            let pixels = Double(max(width, 1)) * Double(max(height, 1))
127	            let rateFactor = fps.double > 30.5 ? 1.5 : 1.0
128	            // HEVC reaches the same picture at roughly 60 % of H.264's rate —
129	            // the ratio between the two 1080p rungs of the same Apple
130	            // specification the tiers are calibrated against. AV1 takes
131	            // HEVC's factor (spec §11 CX-9 (2)): its efficiency goes to the
132	            // picture, not the file size. VP9 takes it too (CX-9 (2), CX-16 (7)).
133	            let lower = codec.lowercased()
134	            let codecFactor = QualityTier.isHEVC(codec) || lower == "av1" || lower == "vp9"
135	                ? 0.6 : 1.0
136	            let bits = pixels * 30 * bitsPerPixel * rateFactor * codecFactor
137	            // To the nearest 100 kbps: these are estimates, and a request for
138	            // "7 963 200 bits" would claim a precision they do not have.
139	            return max(100_000, Int((bits / 100_000).rounded()) * 100_000)
140	        }
141	
142	        private static func isHEVC(_ codec: String) -> Bool {
143	            let codec = codec.lowercased()
144	            return codec.hasPrefix("hevc") || codec.hasPrefix("h265") || codec.hasPrefix("h.265")
145	        }
146	    }
147	
148	    /// The tiers, in menu order. Index 0 of the popup is "Format default",
149	    /// i.e. no override at all — the format's own rate, or the export
150	    /// session's ladder when it carries none.
151	    static let tiers: [QualityTier] = [
152	        QualityTier(name: "Low", bitsPerPixel: 0.064, audioBitsPerSecond: 128_000),
153	        QualityTier(name: "Medium", bitsPerPixel: 0.096, audioBitsPerSecond: 192_000),
154	        QualityTier(name: "High", bitsPerPixel: 0.129, audioBitsPerSecond: 256_000),
155	        QualityTier(name: "Maximum", bitsPerPixel: 0.193, audioBitsPerSecond: 320_000),
156	    ]
157	
158	    /// What the picked format can actually take from this sheet.
159	    ///
160	    /// Both the enablement of every control AND every override key are read
161	    /// from one of these, so a greyed-out control can never still be sending
162	    /// a value to the core — which is what keeps the sheet honest as formats
163	    /// that are not H.264 movies join the list.
164	    struct Applies {
165	        private let preset: ExportPreset?
166	
167	        init(_ preset: ExportPreset?) {
168	            self.preset = preset
169	        }
170	
171	        /// A frame sequence — GIF or APNG — has a size and a frame rate but
172	        /// no bit rate to spend and no audio track to put one on.
173	        private var frameSequence: Bool {
174	            guard let preset = preset else { return false }
175	            return ExportSheetController.isFrameSequence(container: preset.container)
176	        }
177	
178	        /// A row whose data rate is not the sheet's to name. ProRes is a
179	        /// fixed-rate intra codec — the profile decides — and §7.8's preset
180	        /// pairs it with LPCM audio; the two LPCM audio rows are
181	        /// uncompressed by definition, so offering either of them an AAC bit
182	        /// rate would be a control that changes nothing about the file. Both
183	        /// are `ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec:)`.
184	        private var fixedRate: Bool {
185	            ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec: preset?.codec ?? "")
186	        }
187	
188	        private var hasVideo: Bool { preset.map { !$0.audioOnly } ?? false }
189	
190	        var size: Bool { hasVideo }
191	        var frameRate: Bool { hasVideo }
192	        var videoBitrate: Bool { hasVideo && !frameSequence && !fixedRate }
193	        var audioBitrate: Bool { preset != nil && !frameSequence && !fixedRate }
194	        var quality: Bool { videoBitrate || audioBitrate }
195	
196	        /// Loudness normalisation is a gain on the mixed sound, so it
197	        /// applies to every row that HAS sound — which is every row but the
198	        /// two frame sequences. Deliberately not gated by `fixedRate` (ProRes
199	        /// carries LPCM audio and takes a gain like anything else) nor by
200	        /// `hasVideo` (the three audio-only rows are exactly where a
201	        /// delivery target matters most).
202	        var loudness: Bool { preset != nil && !frameSequence }
203	
204	        /// The Dynamic Range popup is live only on a row that carries an HLG
205	        /// project's HDR picture (spec §11 HD-14 (h)).
206	        var dynamicRange: Bool { preset?.carriesHDR ?? false }
207	
208	        /// The Speed popup is live only on a row whose bundled encoder has
209	        /// speeds (spec §11 CX-12 (2); not `vp9_webm`, CX-16 (2)).
210	        var encoderSpeed: Bool { !(preset?.encoderSpeeds.isEmpty ?? true) }
211	
212	        /// The Bit depth popup is live only on a row that lists depths: the
213	        /// uncompressed WAV and AIFF rows (spec §11 AU-29).
214	        var audioBits: Bool { !(preset?.audioBits.isEmpty ?? true) }
215	
216	        /// The Stems popup is live only on a row that lists modes: the three
217	        /// audio rows (spec §11 AU-108 (a)).
218	        var stems: Bool { !(preset?.stems.isEmpty ?? true) }
219	
220	        /// The video rate is a soft cap on every row a bundled encoder writes
221	        /// (spec §11 CX-13, CX-16 (7)), whether or not it has speeds.
222	        var softCap: Bool { preset?.writer != nil }
223	    }
224	
225	    /// GIF and APNG. Spelled once, and taken from the container rather than
226	    /// the codec because that is the field both `ExportPreset` and
227	    /// `ExportSettings` carry.
228	    static func isFrameSequence(container: String) -> Bool {
229	        let container = container.lowercased()
230	        return container == "gif" || container == "apng"
231	    }
232	
233	    /// A bit rate as the tier rows and the footnote spell it.
234	    static func rateText(_ bitsPerSecond: Int) -> String {
235	        if bitsPerSecond >= 1_000_000 {
236	            return String(format: "%.1f Mbps", Double(bitsPerSecond) / 1_000_000)
237	        }
238	        return "\(Int((Double(bitsPerSecond) / 1000).rounded())) kbps"
239	    }
240	}

243	/// The export sheet's SAVED PRESETS: the popup that lists them, the gear that
244	/// saves and deletes one, and the rule that a hand change to any control drops
245	/// the popup back to "Custom".

247	/// A fourth file for one card, and it is the same payment the other three
248	/// record: `ExportSheetController.swift` stood at the ~600-line cap and had to
249	/// give something up before it took this on. The seam is a clean one. The
250	/// controller BUILDS the card's controls and commits it; `Options` is what a
251	/// control means before any of them is read; `Resolve` turns a selection into
252	/// the core's answer and back; and this file owns the LIST — a thing that
253	/// outlives the sheet, lives in a file in Application Support, and is the only
254	/// part of the card with a store behind it. Nothing here computes an export
255	/// setting, and nothing here reads one.
256	///
257	/// What a preset IS lives next to the file that holds it
258	/// (`ExportPresetsStore.swift`), and applying one is `Resolve`'s `apply(_:)` —
259	/// the same method the remembered choice goes through, which is what makes a
260	/// saved preset provably the same thing as clicking each control by hand.
261	///

263	/// `presetEdited()` and `presetChanged(_:)` are internal because `loadView` and
264	/// the control actions in the controller call them, and every stored control
265	/// they touch was already internal for the same reason. `saveChoice` and
266	/// `deleteChoice` are internal for a different one, and it is the reason they
267	/// exist as a pair separate from the two gear items: the items run an app-modal
268	/// alert and a menu, neither of which a headless script can answer, so the two
269	/// WRITES sit under them where a probe compiled from `app/Sources` can drive
270	/// what the file actually does.

272	
273	    /// The Preset popup and its gear, together on one row: 216 + 6 + 36 fits
274	    /// the 318 points the 480-wide card leaves beside its 106 label column.
275	    /// The card's width is the owner's (`cardWidth`, #243), not this row's:
276	    /// the row fitted the 420-wide card it was built on exactly.

278	        sheetRow([presetPopup, presetMenuButton])
279	    }

281	    /// The gear: a pull-down, whose item 0 is its own face rather than a row.

283	    /// `autoenablesItems` stays ON and `validateMenuItem` answers for Delete.
284	    /// The pitfall recorded for the Remove Silences sheet is the same
285	    /// mechanism read the other way — a popup's menu validates its own rows,
286	    /// so an item disabled by hand is switched straight back on unless
287	    /// autoenabling is turned off first. Rather than turn it off and then
288	    /// re-synchronise Delete from four places, this uses the validation it
289	    /// would have been fighting.
290	    func buildPresetMenuButton() {
291	        let menu = NSMenu()
292	        let face = NSMenuItem()
293	        face.image = NSImage(systemSymbolName: "gearshape", accessibilityDescription: "Presets")?
294	            .withSymbolConfiguration(NSImage.SymbolConfiguration(pointSize: 11, weight: .regular))

296	        // the image-only position has to go with the image, or the fallback

299	            face.title = "⋯"
300	        } else {

302	        }

326	                let item = NSMenuItem(title: choice.name, action: nil, keyEquivalent: "")
327	                item.representedObject = choice
328	                menu.addItem(item)

425	            return

430	            NSSound.beep()
431	            return

453	    /// whether the write landed, so the caller can beep.
454	    ///
455	    /// **The store is re-READ here rather than written from the snapshot the
456	    /// sheet opened with**, and that is the whole of these two methods.
457	    /// `userPresets` is loaded once per controller and a controller is built
458	    /// per ⌘E, so one window that opens, saves and closes is always current —
459	    /// but a sheet is WINDOW-modal, two documents can hold two cards at once
460	    /// (and two app instances one file), and `write()` replaces the file
461	    /// whole. Saving "Master" from a card whose snapshot predates the other
462	    /// window's "Web" would have written a file holding only "Master", with
463	    /// "Web" still listed in the popup that had just saved it — exactly the
464	    /// promise `savePreset` makes and cannot keep from a stale value. Reading
465	    /// first costs one small file read per Save… and brings the other
466	    /// window's additions into this popup for free.
467	    ///
468	    /// What re-reading cannot fix is the OTHER card's popup, which goes on
469	    /// listing a preset this one deleted until it is rebuilt. That is display

476	    /// app-modal alert, which no headless script can answer.

548	/// The export sheet's CONTROL CHOICES as a value, and the two places they are
549	/// kept: the last one used (`UserDefaults`) and the named ones a person saves
550	/// (`~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/ExportPresets.json`).
551	///
552	/// **A stored preset is what the CONTROLS said, never what the core resolved,
553	/// and that is the whole design.** Road map 2's phase 7 asks for "a name →
554	/// overrides map … resolved by the core's `export_settings` like any
555	/// overrides, so the core never learns about them". The last clause stands and
556	/// is why this file has no `rc_*` call in it and needs none. The first cannot
557	/// be built, for two independent reasons:
558	///
559	/// 1. **The encoding is not an override.** `rc_export_settings` takes the
560	///    preset id as a separate ARGUMENT, and `export_overrides.rs` has no
561	///    `preset` key — it ignores a key it does not know, silently, on purpose —
562	///    so a map that carried the format would drop it and every preset would
563	///    resolve as H.264.
564	/// 2. **A resolved map cannot restore the sheet.** The Quality popup stores a
565	///    bits-per-pixel TIER and derives a bit rate at pick time from the frame
566	///    the controls are asking for; the Size popup stores a ROW ID
567	///    (`export_size.rs`'s vocabulary). Handed back
568	///    `{width: 1920, height: 1080, video_bitrate: 8000000}` the sheet cannot
569	///    tell "1080p + High" from "Custom 1920 × 1080 + a typed rate" — and
570	///    re-applying an absolute bit rate on a document of another size silently
571	///    changes what "High" meant, which is exactly what a tier expressed in
572	///    bits per PIXEL exists to prevent.
573	///
574	/// So a preset is the row of choices a person made, and applying one is the
575	/// same code path as picking each control by hand: `ExportSheetController`'s
576	/// `apply(_:)` writes the controls, `overrides()` turns them into the core's
577	/// object, and `rc_export_settings` answers. Nothing here computes a size, a
578	/// rate or a duration, which is the §7 rule the whole sheet is built on.
579	///
580	/// The consequence worth knowing, because it is a FEATURE: a preset saved on a
581	/// 1080p document and applied to a 4K one exports 4K at the tier's rate for
582	/// 4K. It remembers the request, not the answer.
583	struct ExportChoice: Codable, Equatable {
584	    /// The preset's name as the popup lists it. Empty for the remembered
585	    /// choice, which is nobody's preset and is never listed — the field is
586	    /// part of the record because the FILE's shape is a flat list of named
587	    /// choices, and splitting the type in two to keep one string out of one
588	    /// of its two homes would buy nothing.
589	    var name: String = ""
590	
591	    /// `ExportPreset.id` — the core's own vocabulary for the encoding
592	    /// (`export_table.rs`), so a row renamed in the table still restores.
593	    var presetID: String = ""
594	
595	    /// `ExportSize.id` — "document", "1080p", "preset"… — and never an
596	    /// INDEX. `visibleSizes` drops every row whose numbers an earlier row
597	    /// already has, so index 2 names a different size on a vertical document
598	    /// than on a landscape one; the id is stable across both.
599	    var sizeRow: String?
600	
601	    /// `[width, height]` when "Custom…" was chosen. Exclusive with
602	    /// `sizeRow` in practice, and if a hand-edited file carries both the row
603	    /// wins, because a row is a thing the sheet can select and a custom size
604	    /// is only reachable through it.
605	    var customSize: [Int]?
606	
607	    /// `[num, den]`, or nil for "Project rate" — the popup's first row, which
608	    /// is no override at all.
609	    var fps: [Int]?
610	
611	    /// `QualityTier.name` ("Low", "Medium", "High", "Maximum"), or nil for
612	    /// "Format default". The NAME and not the derived bit rate: see the type
613	    /// doc's second reason.
614	    var qualityTier: String?
615	
616	    /// The integrated loudness target in LUFS, or nil for "Off".
617	    ///
618	    /// The number rather than the popup ROW, though the contract allows
619	    /// either. Restoring picks the matching row when there is one and
620	    /// "Custom…" otherwise, so a target of −16 comes back as the −16 row even
621	    /// if it was typed into the Custom field. That is a difference in which
622	    /// control is lit and in nothing else: `overrides()` reads the same
623	    /// number out of either state, so the file that gets written is
624	    /// identical, and one number cannot disagree with itself the way a row
625	    /// plus a value can.
626	    var loudness: Double?
627	
628	    /// True for "In/out range". Degrades to "Whole project" on a document
629	    /// that has no range — the popup only carries that row when it does.
630	    var inOutRange: Bool = false
631	
632	    /// The burn-in checkbox. It is a RECIPE option rather than an export
633	    /// override (`RecipeOptions`), but from this sheet's side it is one more
634	    /// control, and a preset that remembered every choice but that one would
635	    /// be a preset that quietly stopped burning in.
636	    var burnInTimecode: Bool = false
637	
638	    /// The Speed popup's last word (`EncoderSpeed`, spec §11 CX-12 (2)), stored on every
639	    /// row so the popup keeps it across formats; only `av1` sends it.
640	    var encoderSpeed: String?
641	
642	    /// The Bit depth popup's last choice (16 or 24, spec §11 AU-29), stored on every row so
643	    /// the popup keeps it across formats; only `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` send it.
644	    var audioBits: Int?
645	
646	    /// The Stems popup's last word ("tracks" or "names", nil for None, spec §11 AU-108),
647	    /// stored on every row so the popup keeps it across formats; only the audio rows send it.
648	    var stems: String?
649	
650	    /// The file's spelling. Snake case because a person can open
651	    /// `ExportPresets.json` in an editor, and because `burn_in_timecode` is
652	    /// then the same string the core's recipe options use — one name for one
653	    /// idea, even across the FFI it never crosses.
654	    private enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
655	        case name
656	        case presetID = "preset_id"
657	        case sizeRow = "size_row"
658	        case customSize = "custom_size"
659	        case fps
660	        case qualityTier = "quality_tier"
661	        case loudness
662	        case inOutRange = "in_out_range"
663	        case burnInTimecode = "burn_in_timecode"
664	        case encoderSpeed = "encoder_speed"
665	        case audioBits = "audio_bits"
666	        case stems
667	    }
668	
669	    init(
670	        name: String = "", presetID: String = "", sizeRow: String? = nil,
671	        customSize: [Int]? = nil, fps: [Int]? = nil, qualityTier: String? = nil,
672	        loudness: Double? = nil, inOutRange: Bool = false, burnInTimecode: Bool = false,
673	        encoderSpeed: String? = nil, audioBits: Int? = nil, stems: String? = nil
674	    ) {
675	        self.name = name
676	        self.presetID = presetID
677	        self.sizeRow = sizeRow
678	        self.customSize = customSize
679	        self.fps = fps
680	        self.qualityTier = qualityTier
681	        self.loudness = loudness
682	        self.inOutRange = inOutRange
683	        self.burnInTimecode = burnInTimecode
684	        self.encoderSpeed = encoderSpeed
685	        self.audioBits = audioBits
686	        self.stems = stems
687	    }
688	
689	    /// Every key optional, every absence a default.
690	    ///
691	    /// Written by hand rather than synthesized because the synthesized
692	    /// decoder THROWS on a missing non-optional, and this record is read from
693	    /// a file a person can edit and from a defaults value an older build
694	    /// wrote. One missing `burn_in_timecode` would otherwise fail the whole
695	    /// array's decode and take every other preset down with it — the shape of
696	    /// failure `load()` promises never to have.
697	    init(from decoder: Decoder) throws {
698	        let c = try decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
699	        name = (try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .name)) ?? ""
700	        presetID = (try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .presetID)) ?? ""
701	        sizeRow = try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .sizeRow)
702	        customSize = try? c.decodeIfPresent([Int].self, forKey: .customSize)
703	        fps = try? c.decodeIfPresent([Int].self, forKey: .fps)
704	        qualityTier = try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .qualityTier)
705	        loudness = try? c.decodeIfPresent(Double.self, forKey: .loudness)
706	        inOutRange = (try? c.decodeIfPresent(Bool.self, forKey: .inOutRange)) ?? false
707	        burnInTimecode = (try? c.decodeIfPresent(Bool.self, forKey: .burnInTimecode)) ?? false
708	        encoderSpeed = try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .encoderSpeed)
709	        audioBits = try? c.decodeIfPresent(Int.self, forKey: .audioBits)
710	        stems = try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .stems)
711	    }
712	}

717	    /// The `UserDefaults` key the sheet reopens from.
718	    ///
719	    /// ONE key holding the whole record as JSON, rather than nine keys. The
720	    /// record is already a value that has to survive as a unit — half a
721	    /// remembered choice (a format from today, a size from a build that spelled
722	    /// its rows differently) is a sheet that lies about what it will export —

732	            !text.isEmpty, let data = text.data(using: .utf8)

738	    /// export is CONFIRMED and never when the sheet is cancelled: a card
739	    /// somebody opened, fiddled with and dismissed is not a choice they made.
740	    /// The name is dropped, because the remembered choice is nobody's preset.

745	            let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)

753	/// The named export presets, as a value: read the file, ask it questions, hand
754	/// back a NEW store with one more or one fewer, write it out.
755	///
756	/// `AudioNormalize.swift`'s shape applied to a preferences file — peaks in, ops
757	/// out; here, a file in, a list out — and for the same reason: the sheet's
758	/// Save… button and any later caller (the export queue, an agent) provably do
759	/// the same thing to the same list, because there is one implementation of what
760	/// "saving a preset" means and it has no `NSPopUpButton` in it.
761	///
762	/// **Every failure degrades to "no presets".** A missing file, a directory
763	/// where the file should be, a truncated write, a JSON object where an array
764	/// belongs, a record from a newer build: all of them answer an empty store, and
765	/// none of them throws, alerts or interrupts. The list is a convenience over a
766	/// dialog that works perfectly without it, so the worst outcome a corrupt file
767	/// may cause is that the popup is empty — never a lost export, never a crash,
768	/// and never a modal about a preferences file in the middle of somebody's work.
769	struct ExportPresetsStore: Equatable {
770	    /// The file inside `AppSupport.directory`.
771	    static let fileName = "ExportPresets.json"
772	
773	    /// In the order they were first saved. Not sorted: a person's own order is
774	    /// information, and re-saving under an existing name REPLACES that record
775	    /// in place rather than moving it to the end, so the popup does not
776	    /// reshuffle under the pointer.
777	    private(set) var presets: [ExportChoice] = []
778	
779	    static var url: URL? { AppSupport.file(fileName) }
780	
781	    /// The store on disk, or an empty one. See the type doc: there is no
782	    /// failing path out of this.
783	    static func load() -> ExportPresetsStore {
784	        guard let url = url, let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url),
785	            let decoded = try? JSONDecoder().decode([ExportChoice].self, from: data)
786	        else { return ExportPresetsStore() }
787	        var store = ExportPresetsStore()
788	        // A record with no name cannot be listed (the popup is keyed by
789	        // title) and cannot be deleted, so it is dropped rather than shown as
790	        // a blank row. A hand-edited file is the only way to make one.
791	        store.presets = decoded.filter { !Self.normalized($0.name).isEmpty }
792	        return store
793	    }
794	
795	    /// Names compare TRIMMED and case-insensitively, which is the whole of the
796	    /// uniqueness rule. Two presets may not share a name — `NSPopUpButton`
797	    /// aside (its `addItem(withTitle:)` silently REMOVES an existing row with
798	    /// the same title, which is why the sheet builds its menu out of
799	    /// `NSMenuItem`s instead), two rows a person reads as identical are two
800	    /// rows they cannot choose between, and Delete would have to guess which
801	    /// one they meant.
802	    static func normalized(_ name: String) -> String {
803	        name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
804	    }
805	
806	    private static func matches(_ a: String, _ b: String) -> Bool {
807	        normalized(a).caseInsensitiveCompare(normalized(b)) == .orderedSame
808	    }
809	
810	    func preset(named name: String) -> ExportChoice? {
811	        presets.first { Self.matches($0.name, name) }
812	    }
813	
814	    /// A store with `choice` in it, under its own (trimmed) name.
815	    ///
816	    /// An existing name is REPLACED in place — the same name means the same
817	    /// preset, so saving over one is an update and not a second row. The sheet
818	    /// says so before it asks; this is where it is true.
819	    func saving(_ choice: ExportChoice) -> ExportPresetsStore {
820	        var stored = choice
821	        stored.name = Self.normalized(choice.name)
822	        guard !stored.name.isEmpty else { return self }
823	        var store = self
824	        if let index = store.presets.firstIndex(where: { Self.matches($0.name, stored.name) }) {
825	            store.presets[index] = stored
826	        } else {
827	            store.presets.append(stored)
828	        }
829	        return store
830	    }
831	
832	    func removing(named name: String) -> ExportPresetsStore {
833	        var store = self
834	        store.presets.removeAll { Self.matches($0.name, name) }
835	        return store
836	    }
837	
838	    /// Writes the list, creating `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/` at
839	    /// `0700` (`AppSupport.ensureDirectory`) if this is the first thing to
840	    /// need it. Answers whether it landed, so a caller can beep; it never
841	    /// throws, for the reason the type doc gives.
842	    @discardableResult
843	    func write() -> Bool {
844	        guard let url = Self.url, let directory = AppSupport.directory else { return false }
845	        guard (try? AppSupport.ensureDirectory(directory)) != nil else { return false }
846	        let encoder = JSONEncoder()
847	        // Sorted keys and an indent so the file is diffable and readable by
848	        // the person whose Library it is in — it is a preferences file, not a
849	        // wire format, and nothing reads it hot.
850	        encoder.outputFormatting = [.prettyPrinted, .sortedKeys]
851	        guard let data = try? encoder.encode(presets) else { return false }
852	        return (try? data.write(to: url, options: .atomic)) != nil
853	    }
854	}

858	/// after Bit depth, offering None, One per Track and One per Track Name — files beside the
859	/// mix, each a track's sound before the master — None the default. It is live only on a row
860	/// that lists modes (`ExportPreset.stems`, the three audio rows); on every other row it is
861	/// disabled and shows the last choice, as Bit depth does, and sends no override. The choice

866	        ("None", nil), ("One per Track", "tracks"), ("One per Track Name", "names"),

887	        resolveCard()
888	    }

890	    /// The `stems` override: the choice on a row that takes one, nil elsewhere.
891	    func stemsOverride() -> String? {
892	        Applies(currentPreset).stems ? stemsChoice : nil
893	    }
894	
895	    /// The popup follows the format: live on a row that lists modes, disabled elsewhere,
896	    /// showing the choice either way.
897	    func syncStems(_ applies: Applies) {
898	        stemsPopup.isEnabled = applies.stems
899	        let shown = stemsPopup.itemArray.first {

905	    /// A stored choice's mode, None when it names none (or one this build lacks).

3	/// The sheet that stays up for the write itself: a bar, a Cancel that really
4	/// stops the session, and — once the file lands — the result and a Show in
5	/// Finder (spec §10 step 10).
6	///
7	/// It owns the `Exporter`, which is why the export survives everything the
8	/// editor does next: the sheet is retained by the presenting controller for
9	/// as long as it is on screen, and nothing else holds the session.
10	///
11	/// Its own file rather than the foot of `ExportSheetController.swift`, which
12	/// stood at 1114 lines against app/CLAUDE.md's ~600 cap. The seam is where
13	/// the two sheets stop having anything in common: the settings card is a
14	/// conversation with the core — every number it shows comes back from
15	/// `rc_export_settings`, and its controls only decide what to ask for — and
16	/// this one has already finished asking. It holds a project handle, a URL and
17	/// an `Exporter`, watches one number climb, and turns into its own result
18	/// panel; nothing on it can change what is being written.
19	///
20	/// Being a separate CLASS is what makes the cut free. `private` on an
21	/// extension member reaches only its own file, so splitting a type across
22	/// files costs every crossing member its privacy — the price
23	/// `ExporterLoudness.swift` records paying, and the price the two `extension
24	/// ExportSheetController` files beside this one pay. A type carries its own
25	/// scope, so every member below keeps the visibility it had, and
26	/// `EditorViewController+Export.swift` presenting it is the only name that
27	/// crosses.
28	final class ExportProgressSheetController: NSViewController {
29	    private let exporter = Exporter()
30	    /// The project handle as the export was confirmed. Handles are immutable
31	    /// (spec §5.5), so edits made after this point cannot reach the file.
32	    private let project: ReelProject
33	    private let urls: [UInt32: URL]
34	    private let settings: ExportSettings
35	    private let destination: URL
36	    /// What the export asks of the RECIPE rather than of the settings — the
37	    /// timecode burn-in (spec §7.3, road map 2's phase 7). It is a separate
38	    /// argument because it is a separate question: `ExportSettings` is what
39	    /// `rc_export_settings` resolved, and an option posted through the
40	    /// override table would be dropped in silence and the file reported a
41	    /// success. Defaulted, so a caller that does not burn in is written the
42	    /// way it always was.
43	    private let options: RecipeOptions
44	    /// The document's compiled graphics as the export was confirmed (G-13),
45	    /// pinned by `Exporter.export` for the write.
46	    private let graphics: GraphicSet?
47	
48	    private let bar = NSProgressIndicator()

215	/// The export card's two commits, Export… and Add to Queue, which end in a save panel and hand
216	/// the resolved settings to the editor: `commit(queue:)` with the three button actions that
217	/// reach it, `recipeOptions`, `suggestedName` and `panelMessage`. An extension of
218	/// `ExportSheetController` in a file of its own, a pure move out of the controller before the
219	/// HDR road map's export range (hdr H-0).
220	extension ExportSheetController {
221	    // MARK: - Commit
222	
223	    @objc func cancelClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
224	        dismiss(self)
225	    }
226	
227	    /// Export… — write it now, behind a progress sheet.
228	    @objc func exportClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
229	        commit(queue: false)
230	    }
231	
232	    /// Add to Queue — write it later, behind nothing. The SAME commit, in one
233	    /// method, so the buttons cannot drift (road map 2's phase 7e).
234	    @objc func queueClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
235	        commit(queue: true)
236	    }
237	
238	    /// Hands off to the save panel, then to `EditorViewController`'s
239	    /// `beginExport` — or, for Add to Queue, its `enqueueExport`. The settings
240	    /// are captured BEFORE the dismissal: after it this controller's window is
241	    /// gone and its controls are on their way out of the view tree. Everything
242	    /// above the handoff is the same for both buttons and is written once for
243	    /// that reason: a queued job is not a second kind of export, it is this
244	    /// one held until its turn.
245	    private func commit(queue: Bool) {
246	        // End any edit in a Custom field first. A mouse click on a button
247	        // does not take the first responder from a text field, so the value
248	        // typed there has not been committed — `controlTextDidEndEditing`,
249	        // and the resolve it runs, fire only when the field editor resigns —
250	        // and `resolved` still describes the size from BEFORE the edit.
251	        // Handing the first responder to nobody makes it resign now,
252	        // synchronously, so the read below sees the numbers on screen. A
253	        // field whose text its formatter rejects refuses to resign; that is
254	        // the person's to fix, so the click just beeps.
255	        guard endSheetFieldEditing() else { return }
256	        guard let editor = editor, let settings = resolved,
257	              let window = editor.view.window
258	        else {
259	            NSSound.beep()
260	            return
261	        }
262	        // Read while the controls still exist. `recipeOptions` is not part of
263	        // `settings` and never can be: the burn-in changes the PICTURE, so it
264	        // travels with the description of the picture rather than through the
265	        // override table, which drops a key it does not know without a word
266	        // (`RecipeOptions`).
267	        let options = recipeOptions
268	        // Remembered on the COMMIT and not on the dismissal: a card somebody
269	        // opened, fiddled with and cancelled is not a choice they made — and
270	        // queueing a job is as much a choice as exporting one, so both
271	        // buttons record it.
272	        currentChoice.remember()
273	        let name = suggestedName(for: settings, in: editor)
274	        dismiss(self)
275	
276	        let panel = NSSavePanel()
277	        panel.nameFieldStringValue = name
278	        panel.canCreateDirectories = true
279	        panel.isExtensionHidden = false
280	        panel.message = Self.panelMessage(for: settings)
281	        if let type = Exporter.contentType(for: settings) {
282	            panel.allowedContentTypes = [type]
283	        }
284	        // AppKit queues this behind the sheet that is on its way out, so the
285	        // panel appears once the settings card has finished leaving.
286	        panel.beginSheetModal(for: window) { [weak editor] response in
287	            guard response == .OK, let url = panel.url, let editor = editor else { return }
288	            // The handoff, and the only place the two buttons differ. The
289	            // project and its media are read on the far side of it, at the
290	            // moment the destination is known — which for a queued job is the
291	            // whole of what makes it immutable (`ExportQueueController`).
292	            if queue {
293	                editor.enqueueExport(settings: settings, to: url, options: options)
294	            } else {
295	                editor.beginExport(settings: settings, to: url, options: options)
296	            }
297	        }
298	    }
299	
300	    /// What the card asks of the RECIPE rather than of the export settings —
301	    /// today, the burn-in and nothing else.
302	    var recipeOptions: RecipeOptions {
303	        RecipeOptions(burnInTimecode: burnInCheckbox.state == .on)
304	    }
305	
306	    /// The document's name with the container's extension: `displayStem`, the
307	    /// title with the package's own extension off and NOTHING else off, so
308	    /// "Board v1.2" is `Board v1.2.mp4` (`ProjectDocument+DisplayStem.swift`).
309	    private func suggestedName(for settings: ExportSettings, in editor: EditorViewController)
310	        -> String
311	    {
312	        let stem = editor.document?.displayStem ?? ProjectDocument.untitledDisplayName
313	        return stem + "." + Exporter.fileExtension(for: settings)
314	    }

316	    /// The save panel's one line about what is being written. "As a movie"
317	    /// was wrong for half the table: a GIF or an APNG is an animated image
318	    /// and the audio-only row writes no picture at all. The classes are the
319	    /// sheet's own (`Applies`, `isFrameSequence`), so a format that is
320	    /// neither is a movie by the same reading that gave it a Size popup.
321	    private static func panelMessage(for settings: ExportSettings) -> String {
322	        if settings.isAudioOnly { return "Export the timeline's audio." }
323	        if isFrameSequence(container: settings.container) {
324	            return "Export the timeline as an animated \(settings.container.uppercased())."
325	        }
326	        return "Export the timeline as a movie."
327	    }

478	    /// `startWriting()` then fails with `AVFoundationErrorDomain` −11834
479	    /// ("Cannot Encode"), leaving a 0-byte file at the destination. So it is
480	    /// mapped here, where `startWriting` hears the pipeline: exactly that
481	    /// domain and code become `.presetUnavailable` with the preset's name and
482	    /// the file is removed, and every other result is returned as it came.
483	    static func encoderOutcome(

486	        guard case .failure(let error) = result else { return result }
487	        let reason = error as NSError

489	            reason.code == AVError.Code.encoderNotFound.rawValue
490	        else { return result }
491	        try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: destination)
492	        return .failure(ExportError.presetUnavailable(ExportWriter.presetName(settings)))

497	/// Pass one of an export: read the composed mix and MEASURE it (`Loudness.swift`).
498	///
499	/// This is `Exporter`'s own "Measuring the mix" section, in a file of its own
500	/// because `Exporter.swift` went past app/CLAUDE.md's ~600-line cap when phase
501	/// 5 put a second pass in it. It is a MOVE and nothing else — the same methods,
502	/// the same order, the same bodies — so `Exporter.swift`'s five internal members
503	/// (`lock`, `measuring`, `scratchStorage`, `scratchCapacity`, and the
504	/// `isCancelled` / `setMeasureProgress` accessors over that lock) are internal
505	/// only to be reachable from here. Stored properties cannot live in an
506	/// extension, which is the whole reason the split is where it is.
507	///
508	/// **What it buys.** Every export that carries sound gets a measured
509	/// "Peak −1.0 dBTP · −14.0 LUFS" on its final line, and an export that asked to
510	/// be normalised gets the gain that lands it on its target. The pass is a
511	/// reader with no writer, no video output and no encoder — audio decode through
512	/// the plan's own mix, and nothing else — so it costs a few per cent of a movie
513	/// export and roughly doubles an audio-only one, which is also the case where
514	/// the number matters most.
515	///
516	/// **It builds its OWN composition.** An `AVAudioMix` copy shares the
517	/// `MTAudioProcessingTap` objects its input parameters hold, and a tap carries
518	/// per-instance state (the compressor's envelope, the noise reducer's delay
519	/// line), so two readers over one mix would interleave into one tap's. Running
520	/// them strictly in sequence would *probably* survive on `AudioTapContext`'s
521	/// start-of-stream reset — but not for a range shorter than its 0.1 s seek
522	/// tolerance, and a second build costs one more pass of opening asset tracks on
523	/// a queue that exists for exactly that and removes the argument entirely. It is
524	/// the same movie by construction: the same plan JSON, the same media, the same
525	/// recipe slot. Its `videoComposition` is never read. `Exporter.export` is where
526	/// that second build happens; everything below is what it is handed.
527	///
528	/// **Nothing here can fail an export.** Every refusal is a nil, which means "no
529	/// loudness figure" and never "no file": the write pass that follows is the one
530	/// that decides whether there is one.
531	extension Exporter {
532	
533	    // MARK: - Measuring the mix
534	
535	    /// What the measurement READS: `ExportAudioMaster.floatMixSettings`, the
536	    /// one float dictionary, and the same one every export's write pass reads
537	    /// (spec §11 #86, AU-27). So the gain is applied to exactly the signal
538	    /// measured here, and the master limits it.
539	    ///
540	    /// **Why float.** Int16 SATURATES. A mix hotter than full scale — which
541	    /// is exactly the material loudness normalisation exists for — would be
542	    /// measured clipped, and its true peak would be pinned at 0 dBTP by the
543	    /// decode rather than by the signal. Read as float, the overshoot is
544	    /// measured whole and the master holds it at its ceiling.
545	    ///
546	    /// **Why the rate and the channel count are the writer's.** BS.1770-4
547	    /// sums weighted channel powers and left and right both carry 1.0, so
548	    /// the same signal measured as one channel and written as two is 3.01 LU
549	    /// apart. An `AVAssetReaderAudioMixOutput` will happily give one channel
550	    /// to a caller who asks; measuring at a shape the file is not written at
551	    /// is a silent 3 dB error.
552	    private static let measureSampleRate: Double = 48000
553	    private static let measureChannelCount = 2

64	        // preset, but a listing can also fail on its own (a reply this
65	        // build cannot decode), and the size the sheet would then send is
66	        // the fields' clamped floor, 16 × 16, which nobody asked for.
67	        if let message = sizesError {
68	            resolved = nil
69	            resolveError = message
70	            syncReadout()
71	            return
72	        }
73	        // An empty Custom field is not a size. Its formatter accepts the
74	        // empty string as "no value", `integerValue` reads that as 0, and
75	        // the clamp would turn it into the 16-pixel floor — an export
76	        // nobody asked for, reached by clearing a field and clicking
77	        // Export…, since that click commits the field before it reads.
78	        if isCustomSize, currentApplies.size,
79	            widthField.stringValue.isEmpty || heightField.stringValue.isEmpty
80	        {
81	            resolved = nil
82	            resolveError = "Type a width and a height, or pick a size from the list."
83	            syncReadout()
84	            return
85	        }
86	        // The same rule for the Custom loudness field, and for the same
87	        // reason: an empty field is not a target, and reading it as one would
88	        // export at whatever the clamp's floor happens to be.
89	        if isCustomLoudness, currentApplies.loudness, loudnessField.stringValue.isEmpty {
90	            resolved = nil
91	            resolveError = "Type a loudness target in LUFS, or pick one from the list."
92	            syncReadout()
93	            return
94	        }
95	        do {
96	            resolved = try ReelExport.settings(
97	                project, preset: preset.id, overrides: overrides())
98	            resolveError = nil
99	        } catch {
100	            resolved = nil
101	            resolveError = error.localizedDescription
102	        }
103	        syncReadout()
104	    }

108	    /// The controls as an `ExportChoice`, with the sheet's own gating applied:
109	    /// a control the chosen format cannot take (`Applies`) contributes
110	    /// nothing, exactly as it contributes no override. So a preset saved off
111	    /// an audio-only row carries no size, and one saved off a GIF carries no
112	    /// loudness — the record says what was actually asked for and never what
113	    /// a greyed-out popup happened to be sitting on.
114	    ///
115	    /// **The burn-in is gated by that same rule and used not to be**, which
116	    /// broke the sentence above rather than any of the core's: a tick made on
117	    /// an H.264 row and carried across to WAV was written into the record
118	    /// beside a size, an fps and a tier all three deliberately left empty, so
119	    /// a named preset — and the remembered choice, which is this same
120	    /// value — said a file with no picture would carry a burn-in. It is not an
121	    /// override, so nothing downstream ever refused it; `Applies.burnIn`
122	    /// (below) is where it is refused now.
123	    ///
124	    /// The `name` is empty: naming a choice is the Save… item's business.
125	    var currentChoice: ExportChoice {
126	        var choice = ExportChoice(presetID: currentPreset?.id ?? "")
127	        if currentApplies.size {
128	            if isCustomSize {
129	                choice.customSize = [clampedSize(widthField), clampedSize(heightField)]
130	            } else {
131	                let index = sizePopup.indexOfSelectedItem
132	                // The ROW's id, never its index (`ExportChoice.sizeRow`).
133	                // Index 0 is recorded like any other: it is a row a person
134	                // chose, and `sizeOverride()`'s decision to send it as no
135	                // override at all is about the CORE's default and not about
136	                // what the popup was showing.
137	                if index >= 0, index < visibleSizes.count {
138	                    choice.sizeRow = visibleSizes[index].id
139	                }
140	            }
141	        }
142	        choice.fps = currentRate.map { [$0.num, $0.den] }
143	        choice.qualityTier = currentTier?.name
144	        choice.loudness = currentLoudness
145	        choice.inOutRange = rangePopup.indexOfSelectedItem == 1
146	        choice.burnInTimecode = currentApplies.burnIn && recipeOptions.burnInTimecode
147	        choice.encoderSpeed = encoderSpeedChoice.rawValue
148	        choice.audioBits = audioBitsChoice
149	        choice.stems = stemsChoice
150	        return choice
151	    }

153	    /// Writes a stored choice back into the controls. **The order is
154	    /// load-bearing and this method is where it is written down**; every
155	    /// caller — the remembered choice in `loadView`, a preset picked from the
156	    /// popup — goes through here so there is only ever one order.
157	    ///
158	    /// 1. **Format FIRST, before the sizes are listed.** A programmatic
159	    ///    `selectItem` sends no action, so `formatChanged`'s `sizesPreset`
160	    ///    guard never fires and nothing rebuilds on its own; listing after the
161	    ///    pick is what makes the rows this format's rows.
162	    /// 2. **Size AFTER `rebuildSizes()`**, which ends with an unconditional
163	    ///    `sizePopup.selectItem(at: 0)` and would undo a selection made before
164	    ///    it.
165	    /// 3. **A custom LOUDNESS selects "Custom…" first and fills the field
166	    ///    second**, because `syncReadout` overwrites that field from the popup
167	    ///    whenever the popup is not on Custom — and `resolve()` runs one
168	    ///    `syncReadout` after this returns.
169	    /// 4. **`in_out` degrades to "Whole project"** on a document that has no
170	    ///    range: the popup only carries that row when `range != nil`, so
171	    ///    selecting index 1 would select nothing at all.
172	    ///
173	    /// It does NOT resolve. The caller does, once, after the last control has
174	    /// moved — a resolve per control would be six FFI round trips to paint one
175	    /// card.
176	    func apply(_ choice: ExportChoice) {
177	        if let index = presets.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == choice.presetID }) {
178	            formatPopup.selectItem(at: index)
179	        }
180	        rebuildSizes()
181	        applySize(choice)
182	
183	        if let fps = choice.fps, fps.count == 2,
184	            let index = Self.rates.firstIndex(where: { $0.num == fps[0] && $0.den == fps[1] })
185	        {
186	            ratePopup.selectItem(at: index + 1)
187	        } else {
188	            ratePopup.selectItem(at: 0)
189	        }
190	
191	        if let name = choice.qualityTier,
192	            let index = Self.tiers.firstIndex(where: { $0.name == name })
193	        {
194	            qualityPopup.selectItem(at: index + 1)
195	        } else {
196	            qualityPopup.selectItem(at: 0)
197	        }
198	
199	        applyLoudness(choice)
200	        rangePopup.selectItem(at: choice.inOutRange && range != nil ? 1 : 0)
201	        burnInCheckbox.state = choice.burnInTimecode ? .on : .off
202	        applySpeed(choice)
203	        applyAudioBits(choice)
204	        applyStems(choice)
205	    }

207	    /// Step 2, after the listing. A row whose id this format does not offer —
208	    /// a GIF's cap under H.264, or a row `visibleSizes` hid because an earlier
209	    /// row already has its numbers — falls back to the SAME NUMBERS under
210	    /// whatever row does show them, and only then to the format's default.
211	    /// Hiding is a tidiness of the popup's (`visibleSizes`), so a choice of
212	    /// "1080p" on a 1920 × 1080 document has to land on "Document size" rather
213	    /// than be dropped: it is the same export.
214	    private func applySize(_ choice: ExportChoice) {
215	        if let row = choice.sizeRow {
216	            if let index = visibleSizes.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == row }) {
217	                sizePopup.selectItem(at: index)
218	                return
219	            }
220	            if let hidden = sizes.first(where: { $0.id == row }),
221	                let index = visibleSizes.firstIndex(where: {
222	                    $0.width == hidden.width && $0.height == hidden.height
223	                })
224	            {
225	                sizePopup.selectItem(at: index)
226	                return
227	            }
228	            return
229	        }
230	        guard let custom = choice.customSize, custom.count == 2 else { return }
231	        // "Custom…" is the item after the last visible row.
232	        sizePopup.selectItem(at: visibleSizes.count)
233	        widthField.integerValue = custom[0]
234	        heightField.integerValue = custom[1]
235	    }

237	    /// Step 3: the row first, the field second.
238	    private func applyLoudness(_ choice: ExportChoice) {
239	        guard let target = choice.loudness else {
240	            loudnessPopup.selectItem(at: 0)
241	            return
242	        }
243	        if let index = Self.loudnessTargets.firstIndex(of: target) {
244	            loudnessPopup.selectItem(at: index + 1)
245	            return
246	        }
247	        loudnessPopup.selectItem(at: Self.loudnessTargets.count + 1)
248	        loudnessField.doubleValue = target
249	    }

251	    var currentPreset: ExportPreset? {
252	        let index = formatPopup.indexOfSelectedItem
253	        guard index >= 0, index < presets.count else { return nil }
254	        return presets[index]
255	    }

257	    private var currentApplies: Applies { Applies(currentPreset) }
258	
259	    /// True while the Size popup's last item, "Custom…", is chosen — which is
260	    /// also the state of a popup whose listing failed, since Custom is then
261	    /// its only item; harmless, because `resolve()` refuses that case before
262	    /// the fields are read.
263	    var isCustomSize: Bool { sizePopup.indexOfSelectedItem == visibleSizes.count }
264	
265	    /// The frame-rate override, or nil for "Project rate" — and always nil
266	    /// for a preset that has no frames, so a rate picked for a movie cannot
267	    /// follow the user into an audio-only export.
268	    private var currentRate: Fps? {
269	        let index = ratePopup.indexOfSelectedItem - 1
270	        guard currentApplies.frameRate, index >= 0, index < Self.rates.count else { return nil }
271	        return Self.rates[index]
272	    }
273	
274	    /// The quality tier, or nil for "Format default" — and, on the same
275	    /// rule, always nil for a preset that takes no bit rate.
276	    private var currentTier: QualityTier? {
277	        let index = qualityPopup.indexOfSelectedItem - 1
278	        guard currentApplies.quality, index >= 0, index < Self.tiers.count else { return nil }
279	        return Self.tiers[index]
280	    }
281	
282	    /// True while the Loudness popup's last item, "Custom…", is chosen.
283	    var isCustomLoudness: Bool {
284	        loudnessPopup.indexOfSelectedItem == Self.loudnessTargets.count + 1
285	    }
286	
287	    /// The integrated target to normalise to, or nil for "Off" — index 0 of
288	    /// the popup, on the Quality row's established rule that the first item
289	    /// is no override at all. Nil too for a format with no sound, so a target
290	    /// picked for a movie cannot follow the user into a GIF.
291	    private var currentLoudness: Double? {
292	        guard currentApplies.loudness else { return nil }
293	        let index = loudnessPopup.indexOfSelectedItem
294	        if index >= 1, index <= Self.loudnessTargets.count {
295	            return Self.loudnessTargets[index - 1]
296	        }
297	        guard isCustomLoudness, !loudnessField.stringValue.isEmpty else { return nil }
298	        let value = loudnessField.doubleValue
299	        guard value.isFinite else { return nil }
300	        return min(
301	            max(value, Self.loudnessRange.lowerBound), Self.loudnessRange.upperBound)
302	    }
