| Case | The stem's name |
| --- | --- |
| A track with no name | Its header's label: `Mix - Track 3.wav` |
| A `/` or `:` in a track name | Written as `-` |
| A name an earlier stem already has, ignoring case | Its track's label follows: `Mix - vo (Track 2).wav` |
| That name is taken too | A count follows the label: `Mix - vo (Track 2, 2).wav` |

No two stems share a file.

## Overwriting and clean-up

:::caution
An existing file at a stem's name is replaced without asking. The save panel asks only about the mix.
:::

There's one exception. If a stem's file would be one of the project's own media files, the export stops before writing any stem and says so:

> The stem “Mix - Dialogue.wav” would replace media this project uses; export under another name.

The stems are written one after another after the mix, and the progress bar counts them. When it's done, the line reads "Exported “Mix.wav” and 3 stems.", and its loudness figures are the mix's. A row in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) ends its first sentence the same way.

Cancelling, or a failure part-way, removes the mix and every stem already written.

## Stems are pre-master

Each stem holds its tracks' sound exactly as the mix plays it, but before the export's master:

- It keeps the clips' and tracks' volume, pan, fades, ducking and effects, and a track's own [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/).

So the stems added together are the mix, to within the last bit, wherever the master neither raised the level nor limited a peak.

A stem can peak higher than the mix. It's clipped only at full scale.

## Good to know

A stem has no [chapters](/export/chapters/), even in an M4A file. Only the mix carries them.

## With an agent

`export` writes stems too, and `export_status` lists each stem's file when the job is done. An agent has no other way to choose them than the two the sheet offers. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).

## Related

- [Audio-only exports](/export/audio-only/)
- [Export loudness](/export/loudness/)
- [Export bit depth](/export/bit-depth/)

---
title: "Export loudness"
description: Normalise a whole mix to a loudness target, and read what every export reports about its sound.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Streaming services, podcast hosts and broadcasters each ask for a certain loudness. **Loudness:** on the export sheet makes the whole mix land on that target, and every export tells you what its sound measured, whether you normalised it or not.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="Export sheet ▸ Loudness"
  tools={['export', 'export_status']}
/>

## Hit a loudness target

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Export…**.

2. In **Loudness:**, choose a target. The footnote under the sheet shows it, for example "−14 LUFS".

3. Choose **Export…** or **Add to Queue**.

4. When the file is done, read [the loudness line](#what-the-loudness-line-means) to see what it measured.

</Steps>

## The Loudness popup

Loudness is the integrated loudness of the whole mix, measured to ITU-R BS.1770-4.

| Choice | What it's for |
| --- | --- |
| **Off** | No normalisation. The export still goes through the master limiter, measures its sound and reports it. |
| **−14 LUFS (streaming)** | Where the main streaming services normalise. |
| **−16 LUFS** | The usual target for stereo podcasts. |
| **−23 LUFS (broadcast)** | EBU R 128 broadcast delivery. |
| **Custom…** | Any target you type in the field beside the popup, from −70 to 0 LUFS, to one decimal place. |

The popup works on every format with sound, ProRes included. It's greyed out for Animated GIF and Animated PNG, which have no sound.

With **Custom…**, the field starts from the target you had chosen, or −14 after **Off**. While it's empty, the sheet says "Type a loudness target in LUFS, or pick one from the list." and **Export…** is greyed out.

The sheet remembers your choice with the rest of your last export, and a [preset](/export/presets/) stores it.

## How normalisation works

The export measures the real mix first, then applies **one gain** to everything. Levels inside the timeline keep their relationship to each other, so a quiet line stays quieter than a loud one.

The progress line reads "Measuring loudness…" during this pass. It takes a few per cent of the time of a movie export, and roughly doubles the time of an audio-only one.

The gain is worked out through the master limiter, so the file lands on the target even when its loudest peaks would pass the ceiling. Those peaks are turned down, not the whole mix.

The gain can be at most +40 dB, so a target more than 40 dB above the mix lands quieter than you asked. It's rounded to 0.01 dB, so two exports of one project compare.

## The master limiter

Every export with sound goes through a true-peak limiter, normalised or not. It keeps the file's true peak under **−1 dBTP**. A mix that would pass that is limited instead of clipped, whether the cause is loud clips, a crossfade between two loud clips, a nest turned up or an action that raises a clip's volume.

- Sound under the ceiling passes through untouched, sample for sample.
- The limiter looks 3.3 ms ahead and releases over 100 ms. The export takes that delay back, so the sound stays exactly in sync with the picture.
- You can't turn it off, and the sheet fixes the ceiling at −1 dBTP.

:::note
The preview has no master limiter, so a mix that passes −1 dBTP sounds louder while you edit than it does in the file.
:::

## Track compressors in the export

A track's own [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) run before the master, on that track's sound alone, exactly as you set them. The export plays each such track on its own through them and mixes the tracks afterwards.

The measurement for a loudness target hears them too, so the file still lands on the target. A [stem](/export/stems/) of that track includes them.

The master is only the loudness gain and the limiter. There's no master compressor or EQ. To compress the whole mix, [nest](/editing/nests/) everything onto one track and give that track a compressor.

## What the loudness line means

Every export of a file with sound reports what that sound measured, on the [finish line](/export/progress-and-report/#the-finish-report) and in its [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) row.

| Line | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `Peak −1.0 dBTP · −14.0 LUFS` | The true peak and integrated loudness of the file. |
| `Peak … · loudness not measurable` | The sound is too short or too quiet to have a loudness. It needs at least 0.4 s. |
| `Silent` | The sound is digital silence. |
| `… · peaks limited by 8.6 dB` | The master limiter turned the loudest peak down by that much to hold the ceiling. It appears from 0.05 dB. |
| `Peak not measurable (a non-finite sample in the mix)` | A source file holds a sample that isn't a number, so no gain is applied. |

A large "peaks limited by" figure on music can be audible. Turn the clips down, or ask for a lower target.

## Good to know

- Sound with no loudness to measure gets no gain, so a target has no effect on digital silence or on sound that's too short or too quiet.
- If the sound can't be measured at all, the file is written without normalisation and the line has no figures. A timeline with no sound at all has none either.
- The figures describe the mix. Stems aren't measured, and they have no target or limiter.

## With an agent

An agent can choose a different ceiling for the master limiter, from −20 to 0 dBTP, with or without a target, which the sheet doesn't offer. 0 dBTP is the loosest, and there's no way to turn the limiter off. `export_status` answers the line's figures as numbers, and says when the +40 dB limit decided the gain. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).

## Related

- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/)
- [The Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/)
- [Audio stems](/export/stems/)
- [Audio-only exports](/export/audio-only/)

---
title: "Burn in timecode"
description: Draw the project's timecode into an exported picture, so a reviewer's notes point at exact frames.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Burn in timecode draws the project's timecode into the exported picture. Use it for a review copy, so a note about a frame carries the number you'll find on your timeline.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="Export sheet ▸ Burn in timecode"
  tools={['export', 'render_frame']}
/>

## Burn in timecode

Tick **Burn in timecode** on the export sheet. It's off by default.

The timecode appears only in the exported file, never in the preview. It sits centred near the bottom of the picture, on a translucent black plate, on top of everything, captions included.

The box works on every format with a picture, Animated GIF and Animated PNG included. It's greyed out for the audio-only formats.

The sheet remembers it with the rest of your last export, and a [preset](/export/presets/) stores it.

## What the timecode shows

It uses the project's own timecode format, as the toolbar shows it: `HH:MM:SS:FF` or `HH:MM:SS.mmm`, non-drop. See [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/).

It shows **project time**. A file exported from an [in/out range](/export/range/) that starts at 00:00:10:00 begins at 00:00 in a player, but its first frame reads 00:00:10:00. That's the number a reviewer's note needs.

## With an agent

**File ▸ Save Frame…** never offers a burn-in, but an agent can draw it into a single frame with `render_frame`, as well as into an export. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).

## Related

- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
- [Export a range](/export/range/)
- [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/)

---
title: "Export presets"
description: Save the export sheet's choices under a name, and set the whole sheet with one pick in any project.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A preset is a set of export choices you've saved under a name. Pick it and the whole sheet is set, in any project. It's the quick way back to the export you make every week.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where={['Export sheet ▸ Preset', 'Export sheet ▸ the gear beside Preset']}
/>

## Apply a preset

Pick the preset in **Preset:**. Every control is set exactly as if you had clicked it.

The first row is **Custom**, then your presets. Picking **Custom** leaves the sheet as it is.

## Save a preset

<Steps>

1. Set the sheet the way you want it.

2. Click the gear beside **Preset:** and choose **Save…**.

3. Type a name and click **Save**, or **Cancel** to save nothing. The name field starts with the name of the preset now chosen.

</Steps>

Saving under a name that already exists, ignoring case, replaces that preset in its place in the list. New presets go at the end.

Frame Job beeps and saves nothing when:

- The name is empty.
- The name is **Custom**, in any case. It's reserved for the popup's first row.
- The sheet has an error, for example an empty custom field.
- The presets file can't be written.

## Change a preset

Apply it, adjust the controls, and save again under the same name. There's no separate rename: to rename a preset, save it under the new name and delete the old one.

## Delete a preset

Choose the preset in **Preset:**, then choose **Delete** from the gear. **Delete** is available only while a saved preset is chosen, and it doesn't ask you to confirm.

The controls keep the preset's values, so **Save…** under the same name puts it back. It returns at the end of the list.

## What a preset stores

A preset stores the choices on the sheet, not the numbers they resolve to, so it means the same on a project of another size. A preset saved on a 1080p project that says "4K, High" exports at the right 4K size and bit rate on any other project.

It stores:

- Format
- Size row, or the custom size
- Frame rate
- Quality tier
- Loudness
- Range
- Burn in timecode
- Speed
- Bit depth
- Stems

**Dynamic Range** isn't stored.

The format decides what a preset can hold. Size, frame rate, quality, loudness and burn-in aren't stored when the format can't use them, so a preset saved on an audio-only format has no size, and one saved on Animated GIF has no loudness. Applying it puts those controls back on their defaults. Speed, Bit depth and Stems are stored whichever format is chosen.

When a preset meets a different project:

- A range falls back to **Whole project** if the project has no range.
- A size row the format doesn't offer falls back to the row with the same numbers, or else to the format's default.
- A custom size stays those exact numbers.

## Back to Custom

Changing **Format:**, **Size:**, **Frame rate:**, **Quality:**, **Loudness:**, **Range:**, **Burn in timecode** or a custom field puts the popup back on **Custom**. Changing the value back doesn't select the preset again.

**Speed:**, **Bit depth:** and **Stems:** don't do this. After you change one of those three, the popup still shows the preset's name, even though the sheet no longer matches it.

The popup opens on **Custom** each time, even when your remembered choices happen to match a preset.

## The presets file

---
title: "Export presets"
description: Save the export sheet's choices under a name, and set the whole sheet with one pick in any project.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A preset is a set of export choices you've saved under a name. Pick it and the whole sheet is set, in any project. It's the quick way back to the export you make every week.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where={['Export sheet ▸ Preset', 'Export sheet ▸ the gear beside Preset']}
/>

Pick the preset in **Preset:**. Every control is set exactly as if you had clicked it.

The first row is **Custom**, then your presets. Picking **Custom** leaves the sheet as it is.

## Save a preset

<Steps>

1. Set the sheet the way you want it.

2. Click the gear beside **Preset:** and choose **Save…**.

3. Type a name and click **Save**, or **Cancel** to save nothing. The name field starts with the name of the preset now chosen.

</Steps>

Saving under a name that already exists, ignoring case, replaces that preset in its place in the list. New presets go at the end.

Frame Job beeps and saves nothing when:

- The name is empty.
- The name is **Custom**, in any case. It's reserved for the popup's first row.
- The sheet has an error, for example an empty custom field.
- The presets file can't be written.

## Change a preset

Apply it, adjust the controls, and save again under the same name. There's no separate rename: to rename a preset, save it under the new name and delete the old one.

## Delete a preset

Choose the preset in **Preset:**, then choose **Delete** from the gear. **Delete** is available only while a saved preset is chosen, and it doesn't ask you to confirm.

The controls keep the preset's values, so **Save…** under the same name puts it back. It returns at the end of the list.

## What a preset stores

A preset stores the choices on the sheet, not the numbers they resolve to, so it means the same on a project of another size. A preset saved on a 1080p project that says "4K, High" exports at the right 4K size and bit rate on any other project.

It stores:

- Format
- Size row, or the custom size
- Frame rate
- Quality tier
- Loudness
- Range
- Burn in timecode
- Speed
- Bit depth
- Stems

**Dynamic Range** isn't stored.

The format decides what a preset can hold. Size, frame rate, quality, loudness and burn-in aren't stored when the format can't use them, so a preset saved on an audio-only format has no size, and one saved on Animated GIF has no loudness. Applying it puts those controls back on their defaults. Speed, Bit depth and Stems are stored whichever format is chosen.

When a preset meets a different project:

- A range falls back to **Whole project** if the project has no range.
- A size row the format doesn't offer falls back to the row with the same numbers, or else to the format's default.
- A custom size stays those exact numbers.

Changing **Format:**, **Size:**, **Frame rate:**, **Quality:**, **Loudness:**, **Range:**, **Burn in timecode** or a custom field puts the popup back on **Custom**. Changing the value back doesn't select the preset again.

**Speed:**, **Bit depth:** and **Stems:** don't do this. After you change one of those three, the popup still shows the preset's name, even though the sheet no longer matches it.

---
title: "Export progress and the report"
description: Follow an export as it writes, cancel it, read its finish report, and find out why one failed.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

After you choose **Export…** on the export sheet, Frame Job asks where to save, then writes the file behind a progress sheet. When it's done, the sheet tells you what the file holds and what went wrong, if anything did.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="The Exporting sheet"
  tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
/>

**Add to Queue** opens the same save panel, then writes the file behind the editor so you can keep working. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).

## The save panel

The save panel suggests the project's name with the format's extension, such as `Board v1.2.mp4`. Its message says what's being written:

| Format | Message |
| --- | --- |
| A movie | "Export the timeline as a movie." |
| Animated GIF | "Export the timeline as an animated GIF." |
| Animated PNG | "Export the timeline as an animated APNG." |
| Audio only | "Export the timeline's audio." |

Cancelling the save panel writes nothing. The export sheet has already closed by then, and it keeps the choices you made for next time.

## The Exporting sheet

**Exporting** shows a progress bar, a percentage and a status line. The status line moves through these:

| Status line | What's happening |
| --- | --- |
| "Preparing “*name*”…" | Frame Job is getting everything ready, and may be waiting for something the file needs. |
| "Measuring loudness…" | The sound is being [measured](/export/loudness/#how-normalisation-works). Every export with sound does this, whether or not you chose a target. |
| "Writing “*name*”…" | The file is being written. |

The file is written from the timeline as it was when you confirmed it.

### While it says Preparing

An export never leaves out something that isn't ready, so it waits for these first:

- The person and foreground masks of every [Remove Background](/export/what-an-export-includes/) clip in the range. This wait has no time limit. Animated GIF and Animated PNG exports wait for masks too.
- Each clip's pointer, from its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/).
- The measured loudness of every clip with a gate, leveller or de-esser, for up to five minutes.
- The rendered sound of speed ramps, clips at another speed with Keep pitch off, [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) and [voice effects](/audio/voice-effects/).

GIF and APNG files have no sound, so they don't wait for the last two. You can cancel during any of these waits.

## Cancel a running export

Choose **Cancel**. The status line reads "Stopping…" until the export has stopped, then the sheet closes and the half-written file is removed.

:::caution
If you chose to replace an existing file in the save panel, that file is gone once you cancel. Cancelling doesn't bring it back.
:::

## The finish report

When an export finishes, the status line names the file and says what the sound measured:

> Exported “name.mp4”. Peak −1.0 dBTP · −14.0 LUFS.

[What the loudness line means](/export/loudness/#what-the-loudness-line-means) explains those figures. A file with no sound has no figures. An export with [stems](/export/stems/) counts them after the name: "Exported “Mix.wav” and 3 stems."

**Show in Finder** reveals the file and closes the sheet. **Close** closes the sheet.

## Graphic and cursor warnings

A warning doesn't stop an export. The finish line adds a count, and its tooltip lists each warning.

| Warning | What happened | What the tooltip lists |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "1 graphic warning (hover for details)." | A [graphic](/graphics/overview/) warned while the file was drawn. | Each warning, with the graphic's name and its frame. |
| "1 cursor warning (hover for details)." | A clip's cursor file couldn't be drawn, so that clip is written without its pointer. | Each one, for example "The cursor of media 3 is not drawn: …" |

The cursor count comes after the graphic count. A finished row in the Export Queue shows the same counts, and its tooltip lists the same warnings.

## Failures

An export that can't run says why in a sentence, on the sheet or on its queue row. On the sheet, **Close** dismisses it.

| The sheet says | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| "There is nothing on the timeline to export — add a clip first." | Add a clip. |
| "The export was not started: the graphic …" | A graphic in the range doesn't compile or has no module. Fix it and export again. |
| "The export was stopped at frame … of the graphic …" | A graphic failed at that frame. No file is left. |
| "Clip … 's loudness or speech has not been measured yet…" | A clip's gate, leveller or de-esser can't be set. Wait for their Status rows to show the clip's loudness, then export again. |
| "Clip …'s retimed audio could not be rendered: …" | The sound of a speed change couldn't be made. |
| "Clip …'s isolated voice could not be rendered: …" | Voice Isolation couldn't be rendered for that clip. |
| "Clip …'s voice effect could not be rendered: …" | The voice effect couldn't be rendered for that clip. |
| "Clip …'s person masks could not be made: …" or "Clip …'s foreground masks could not be made: …" | A Remove Background clip's masks failed. No frame is written without them. |
| "This Mac cannot export with the “…” preset." | This Mac has no encoder for that format. Choose another format. No file is left. |
| "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…" | A custom size has a different shape from the canvas. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). |

Other messages come from macOS or the file being written, and appear as they are.

A failure is different from a cancel. A failed Animated GIF, Animated PNG or WebM export removes its partly written file, and so does a failed export with stems. Any other format that fails while writing can leave a partly written file at the path you chose. It isn't a finished export, so delete it.

## Quitting during an export

Quitting while the Exporting sheet is writing doesn't ask, and leaves the half-written file behind. Cancel the export first.

Only the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) is guarded at quit, so jobs there ask before they stop.

## With an agent

An agent's `export` puts a job on the Export Queue and answers at once, with no progress sheet. A bad argument, a missing folder, an empty timeline or a graphic that doesn't compile comes back from `export` before anything is queued. Failures while writing, the loudness figures and warnings come back from `export_status`, and `cancel_export` stops the job. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).

## Related

- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
- [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/)
- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)
- [Export loudness](/export/loudness/)

input.content:
---
title: "Export a range"
description: Write only the part of the timeline between your in and out points, instead of the whole project.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

An export writes the whole timeline unless you tell it otherwise. Use **Range:** on the export sheet to write only the passage between your in and out points, such as one section of a long project or a clip for review.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="Export sheet ▸ Range"
  tools="export"
/>

## Export only the range

<Steps>

1. On the timeline, set the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) with <kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd>.

2. Choose **File ▸ Export…**.

3. In **Range:**, choose **In/out range**.

4. Check the length in the readout under the controls, then choose **Export…** or **Add to Queue**.

</Steps>

## The Range popup

| Choice | What it writes |
| --- | --- |
| **Whole project** | The whole timeline. This is the default. |
| **In/out range** | Only the range set on the timeline. It's listed only when a range is set. |

With no range set, the popup is greyed out on **Whole project**.

The range is snapped to the export's frame grid and kept inside the project. If you change **Frame rate:**, it lands on that rate's frames, so its length can move by less than a frame. The readout always shows the length the file will have.

The sheet remembers **In/out range** with the rest of your last export, and a [preset](/export/presets/) can store it too. On a project with no range, either one falls back to **Whole project**.

## Inside a nest

An export always writes the top-level timeline, even when you're working inside a [nest](/editing/nests/). So it can't use a range that belongs to a nest.

While a nest is open, the popup is greyed out on **Whole project**. If the nest has a range of its own, the popup's tooltip says why that range isn't offered.

To export that passage, leave the nest with <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> and set the range on the timeline. A range stays with the timeline or nest it was set in, so opening or leaving a nest clears it.

## Sound ends with the range

A file's sound is exactly as long as the range it exports, including when a clip in it plays faster or slower. Frame Job cuts the sound at the range's end, and if the sound runs out early it fills the rest with silence.

## Good to know

- If a range turns out to be empty, for example one that lies past the end of the project after an edit, the sheet says the export range is empty and **Export…** and **Add to Queue** stay greyed out. Set the range again, or choose a different one.
- Animated GIF and Animated PNG files have a limit on their frame count, so a long range may not fit. See [Animated GIF and PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/).
- [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/) reads project time, so a file from a range shows the timeline's timecode, not a count from zero.
- [Chapters](/export/chapters/) explains how a range export treats chapter markers.

## Related

- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)
- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
- [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/)

---
title: "Audio stems"
description: Write each track's sound as its own file beside the mix, for mixing or mastering in another editor.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

An audio export can also write each track's sound as its own file beside the mix. These files are stems. Use them to mix or master the project in another editor.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="Export sheet ▸ Stems"
  tools={['export', 'export_status']}
/>

## Export stems

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Export…**.

2. In **Format:**, choose **Audio only (M4A)**, **Audio only (WAV)** or **Audio only (AIFF)**.

3. In **Stems:**, choose **One per Track** or **One per Track Name**. The footnote under the sheet counts them, for example "3 stems".

4. Choose **Export…** or **Add to Queue**, then name the mix in the save panel.

</Steps>

Frame Job writes the mix, then each stem beside it. The stems are in the same format as the mix and cover the same range.

## The Stems row

| Choice | What it writes |
| --- | --- |
| **None** | The mix alone. This is the default. |
| **One per Track** | The mix, and one stem for each track you can hear. |
| **One per Track Name** | The mix, and one stem for each track name. |

The row sits under **Bit depth:**. On every format except the three audio-only ones it's greyed out and keeps your last choice.

The sheet remembers your choice with the rest of your last export, and a [preset](/export/presets/) stores it.

## Which tracks get a stem

Only tracks you can hear get a stem:

- A [muted track](/audio/mute-and-solo/) has no stem.
- While any track is soloed, only the soloed tracks have one.
- A track with no sound on it, only pictures or nothing, has none.

With **One per Track Name**, tracks whose names match share one file. The match ignores case and any spaces at either end, and the file is named the way the first of those tracks is spelled. A track with no name gets its own file. Name your tracks in [Add, rename and reorder tracks](/timeline/manage-tracks/).

If no track can be heard, the sheet shows "stems: no track is heard, so there is no stem to write", and **Export…** and **Add to Queue** are greyed out.

## Stem file names

A stem is named after the mix and its track, and sits in the same folder. Exporting `Mix.wav` writes `Mix - Dialogue.wav` and `Mix - Music.wav`.

| Case | The stem's name |
| --- | --- |
| A track with no name | Its header's label: `Mix - Track 3.wav` |
| A `/` or `:` in a track name | Written as `-` |
| A name an earlier stem already has, ignoring case | Its track's label follows: `Mix - vo (Track 2).wav` |
| That name is taken too | A count follows the label: `Mix - vo (Track 2, 2).wav` |

No two stems share a file.

## Overwriting and clean-up

:::caution
An existing file at a stem's name is replaced without asking. The save panel asks only about the mix.
:::

There's one exception. If a stem's file would be one of the project's own media files, the export stops before writing any stem and says so:

> The stem “Mix - Dialogue.wav” would replace media this project uses; export under another name.

The stems are written one after another after the mix, and the progress bar counts them. When it's done, the line reads "Exported “Mix.wav” and 3 stems.", and its loudness figures are the mix's. A row in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) ends its first sentence the same way.

Cancelling, or a failure part-way, removes the mix and every stem already written.

## Stems are pre-master

Each stem holds its tracks' sound exactly as the mix plays it, but before the export's master:

- It keeps the clips' and tracks' volume, pan, fades, ducking and effects, and a track's own [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/).
- It gets no [loudness target](/export/loudness/), and the [master limiter](/export/loudness/#the-master-limiter) doesn't touch it.

So the stems added together are the mix, to within the last bit, wherever the master neither raised the level nor limited a peak.

A stem can peak higher than the mix. It's clipped only at full scale.

## Good to know

A stem has no [chapters](/export/chapters/), even in an M4A file. Only the mix carries them.

## With an agent

`export` writes stems too, and `export_status` lists each stem's file when the job is done. An agent has no other way to choose them than the two the sheet offers. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).

## Related

- [Audio-only exports](/export/audio-only/)
- [Export loudness](/export/loudness/)
- [Export bit depth](/export/bit-depth/)

---
title: "Export loudness"
description: Normalise a whole mix to a loudness target, and read what every export reports about its sound.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Streaming services, podcast hosts and broadcasters each ask for a certain loudness. **Loudness:** on the export sheet makes the whole mix land on that target, and every export tells you what its sound measured, whether you normalised it or not.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="Export sheet ▸ Loudness"
  tools={['export', 'export_status']}
/>

## Hit a loudness target

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Export…**.

2. In **Loudness:**, choose a target. The footnote under the sheet shows it, for example "−14 LUFS".

3. Choose **Export…** or **Add to Queue**.

4. When the file is done, read [the loudness line](#what-the-loudness-line-means) to see what it measured.

</Steps>

## The Loudness popup

Loudness is the integrated loudness of the whole mix, measured to ITU-R BS.1770-4.

| Choice | What it's for |
| --- | --- |
| **Off** | No normalisation. The export still goes through the master limiter, measures its sound and reports it. |
| **−14 LUFS (streaming)** | Where the main streaming services normalise. |
| **−16 LUFS** | The usual target for stereo podcasts. |
| **−23 LUFS (broadcast)** | EBU R 128 broadcast delivery. |
| **Custom…** | Any target you type in the field beside the popup, from −70 to 0 LUFS, to one decimal place. |

The popup works on every format with sound, ProRes included. It's greyed out for Animated GIF and Animated PNG, which have no sound.

With **Custom…**, the field starts from the target you had chosen, or −14 after **Off**. While it's empty, the sheet says "Type a loudness target in LUFS, or pick one from the list." and **Export…** is greyed out.

The sheet remembers your choice with the rest of your last export, and a [preset](/export/presets/) stores it.

## How normalisation works

The export measures the real mix first, then applies **one gain** to everything. Levels inside the timeline keep their relationship to each other, so a quiet line stays quieter than a loud one.

The progress line reads "Measuring loudness…" during this pass. It takes a few per cent of the time of a movie export, and roughly doubles the time of an audio-only one.

The gain is worked out through the master limiter, so the file lands on the target even when its loudest peaks would pass the ceiling. Those peaks are turned down, not the whole mix.

The gain can be at most +40 dB, so a target more than 40 dB above the mix lands quieter than you asked. It's rounded to 0.01 dB, so two exports of one project compare.

## The master limiter

Every export with sound goes through a true-peak limiter, normalised or not. It keeps the file's true peak under **−1 dBTP**. A mix that would pass that is limited instead of clipped, whether the cause is loud clips, a crossfade between two loud clips, a nest turned up or an action that raises a clip's volume.

- Sound under the ceiling passes through untouched, sample for sample.
- The limiter looks 3.3 ms ahead and releases over 100 ms. The export takes that delay back, so the sound stays exactly in sync with the picture.
- You can't turn it off, and the sheet fixes the ceiling at −1 dBTP.

:::note
The preview has no master limiter, so a mix that passes −1 dBTP sounds louder while you edit than it does in the file.
:::

## Track compressors in the export

A track's own [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) run before the master, on that track's sound alone, exactly as you set them. The export plays each such track on its own through them and mixes the tracks afterwards.

The measurement for a loudness target hears them too, so the file still lands on the target. A [stem](/export/stems/) of that track includes them.

The master is only the loudness gain and the limiter. There's no master compressor or EQ. To compress the whole mix, [nest](/editing/nests/) everything onto one track and give that track a compressor.

## What the loudness line means

Every export of a file with sound reports what that sound measured, on the [finish line](/export/progress-and-report/#the-finish-report) and in its [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) row.

| Line | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `Peak −1.0 dBTP · −14.0 LUFS` | The true peak and integrated loudness of the file. |
| `Peak … · loudness not measurable` | The sound is too short or too quiet to have a loudness. It needs at least 0.4 s. |
| `Silent` | The sound is digital silence. |
| `… · peaks limited by 8.6 dB` | The master limiter turned the loudest peak down by that much to hold the ceiling. It appears from 0.05 dB. |
| `Peak not measurable (a non-finite sample in the mix)` | A source file holds a sample that isn't a number, so no gain is applied. |

A large "peaks limited by" figure on music can be audible. Turn the clips down, or ask for a lower target.

## Good to know

- Sound with no loudness to measure gets no gain, so a target has no effect on digital silence or on sound that's too short or too quiet.
- If the sound can't be measured at all, the file is written without normalisation and the line has no figures. A timeline with no sound at all has none either.
- The figures describe the mix. Stems aren't measured, and they have no target or limiter.

## With an agent

An agent can choose a different ceiling for the master limiter, from −20 to 0 dBTP, with or without a target, which the sheet doesn't offer. 0 dBTP is the loosest, and there's no way to turn the limiter off. `export_status` answers the line's figures as numbers, and says when the +40 dB limit decided the gain. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).

## Related

- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/)
- [The Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/)
- [Audio stems](/export/stems/)
- [Audio-only exports](/export/audio-only/)

---
title: "Burn in timecode"
description: Draw the project's timecode into an exported picture, so a reviewer's notes point at exact frames.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Burn in timecode draws the project's timecode into the exported picture. Use it for a review copy, so a note about a frame carries the number you'll find on your timeline.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="Export sheet ▸ Burn in timecode"
  tools={['export', 'render_frame']}
/>

## Burn in timecode

Tick **Burn in timecode** on the export sheet. It's off by default.

The timecode appears only in the exported file, never in the preview. It sits centred near the bottom of the picture, on a translucent black plate, on top of everything, captions included.

The box works on every format with a picture, Animated GIF and Animated PNG included. It's greyed out for the audio-only formats.

The sheet remembers it with the rest of your last export, and a [preset](/export/presets/) stores it.

## What the timecode shows

It uses the project's own timecode format, as the toolbar shows it: `HH:MM:SS:FF` or `HH:MM:SS.mmm`, non-drop. See [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/).

It shows **project time**. A file exported from an [in/out range](/export/range/) that starts at 00:00:10:00 begins at 00:00 in a player, but its first frame reads 00:00:10:00. That's the number a reviewer's note needs.

## With an agent

**File ▸ Save Frame…** never offers a burn-in, but an agent can draw it into a single frame with `render_frame`, as well as into an export. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).

## Related

- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
- [Export a range](/export/range/)
- [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/)

---
title: "Export presets"
description: Save the export sheet's choices under a name, and set the whole sheet with one pick in any project.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A preset is a set of export choices you've saved under a name. Pick it and the whole sheet is set, in any project. It's the quick way back to the export you make every week.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where={['Export sheet ▸ Preset', 'Export sheet ▸ the gear beside Preset']}
/>

## Apply a preset

Pick the preset in **Preset:**. Every control is set exactly as if you had clicked it.

The first row is **Custom**, then your presets. Picking **Custom** leaves the sheet as it is.

## Save a preset

<Steps>

1. Set the sheet the way you want it.

2. Click the gear beside **Preset:** and choose **Save…**.

3. Type a name and click **Save**, or **Cancel** to save nothing. The name field starts with the name of the preset now chosen.

</Steps>

Saving under a name that already exists, ignoring case, replaces that preset in its place in the list. New presets go at the end.

Frame Job beeps and saves nothing when:

- The name is empty.
- The name is **Custom**, in any case. It's reserved for the popup's first row.
- The sheet has an error, for example an empty custom field.
- The presets file can't be written.

## Change a preset

Apply it, adjust the controls, and save again under the same name. There's no separate rename: to rename a preset, save it under the new name and delete the old one.

## Delete a preset

Choose the preset in **Preset:**, then choose **Delete** from the gear. **Delete** is available only while a saved preset is chosen, and it doesn't ask you to confirm.

The controls keep the preset's values, so **Save…** under the same name puts it back. It returns at the end of the list.

## What a preset stores

A preset stores the choices on the sheet, not the numbers they resolve to, so it means the same on a project of another size. A preset saved on a 1080p project that says "4K, High" exports at the right 4K size and bit rate on any other project.

It stores:

- Format
- Size row, or the custom size
- Frame rate
- Quality tier
- Loudness
- Range
- Burn in timecode
- Speed
- Bit depth
- Stems

**Dynamic Range** isn't stored.

The format decides what a preset can hold. Size, frame rate, quality, loudness and burn-in aren't stored when the format can't use them, so a preset saved on an audio-only format has no size, and one saved on Animated GIF has no loudness. Applying it puts those controls back on their defaults. Speed, Bit depth and Stems are stored whichever format is chosen.

When a preset meets a different project:

- A range falls back to **Whole project** if the project has no range.
- A size row the format doesn't offer falls back to the row with the same numbers, or else to the format's default.
- A custom size stays those exact numbers.

## Back to Custom

Changing **Format:**, **Size:**, **Frame rate:**, **Quality:**, **Loudness:**, **Range:**, **Burn in timecode** or a custom field puts the popup back on **Custom**. Changing the value back doesn't select the preset again.

**Speed:**, **Bit depth:** and **Stems:** don't do this. After you change one of those three, the popup still shows the preset's name, even though the sheet no longer matches it.

The popup opens on **Custom** each time, even when your remembered choices happen to match a preset.

## The presets file

Presets are kept for your whole account, so every project and window shares them. They live in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/ExportPresets.json`.

You can open the file in a text editor. A damaged file reads as no presets, and the export sheet works as usual.

Saving or deleting reads the file first, so two open sheets can't lose each other's presets. A sheet that's already open keeps listing a preset you've deleted elsewhere until you open it again.

## Good to know

A preset on a transparent format, such as **ProRes 4444 (MOV)** or **HEVC with Alpha (MOV)**, stores the format and nothing about the canvas. The file is transparent only when the project's canvas background is. A custom size also has to match the canvas's shape on these formats, so a preset with a custom size can fail on a canvas of another shape. Use a size row instead, because the rows fit each project's shape. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/).

Presets belong to the sheet. An agent's `export` call doesn't read them, and it names each choice itself.

## Related

- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
- [Choose a format](/export/formats/)
- [Export size](/export/size/)
- [Export quality](/export/quality/)

---
title: "Export progress and the report"
description: Follow an export as it writes, cancel it, read its finish report, and find out why one failed.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

After you choose **Export…** on the export sheet, Frame Job asks where to save, then writes the file behind a progress sheet. When it's done, the sheet tells you what the file holds and what went wrong, if anything did.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="The Exporting sheet"
  tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
/>

**Add to Queue** opens the same save panel, then writes the file behind the editor so you can keep working. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).

## The save panel

The save panel suggests the project's name with the format's extension, such as `Board v1.2.mp4`. Its message says what's being written:

| Format | Message |
| --- | --- |
| A movie | "Export the timeline as a movie." |
| Animated GIF | "Export the timeline as an animated GIF." |
| Animated PNG | "Export the timeline as an animated APNG." |
| Audio only | "Export the timeline's audio." |

Cancelling the save panel writes nothing. The export sheet has already closed by then, and it keeps the choices you made for next time.

## The Exporting sheet

**Exporting** shows a progress bar, a percentage and a status line. The status line moves through these:

| Status line | What's happening |
| --- | --- |
| "Preparing “*name*”…" | Frame Job is getting everything ready, and may be waiting for something the file needs. |
| "Measuring loudness…" | The sound is being [measured](/export/loudness/#how-normalisation-works). Every export with sound does this, whether or not you chose a target. |
| "Writing “*name*”…" | The file is being written. |

The file is written from the timeline as it was when you confirmed it.

### While it says Preparing

An export never leaves out something that isn't ready, so it waits for these first:

- The person and foreground masks of every [Remove Background](/export/what-an-export-includes/) clip in the range. This wait has no time limit. Animated GIF and Animated PNG exports wait for masks too.
- Each clip's pointer, from its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/).
- The measured loudness of every clip with a gate, leveller or de-esser, for up to five minutes.
- The rendered sound of speed ramps, clips at another speed with Keep pitch off, [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) and [voice effects](/audio/voice-effects/).

GIF and APNG files have no sound, so they don't wait for the last two. You can cancel during any of these waits.

## Cancel a running export

Choose **Cancel**. The status line reads "Stopping…" until the export has stopped, then the sheet closes and the half-written file is removed.

:::caution
If you chose to replace an existing file in the save panel, that file is gone once you cancel. Cancelling doesn't bring it back.
:::

## The finish report

When an export finishes, the status line names the file and says what the sound measured:

> Exported “name.mp4”. Peak −1.0 dBTP · −14.0 LUFS.

[What the loudness line means](/export/loudness/#what-the-loudness-line-means) explains those figures. A file with no sound has no figures. An export with [stems](/export/stems/) counts them after the name: "Exported “Mix.wav” and 3 stems."

**Show in Finder** reveals the file and closes the sheet. **Close** closes the sheet.

## Graphic and cursor warnings

A warning doesn't stop an export. The finish line adds a count, and its tooltip lists each warning.

| Warning | What happened | What the tooltip lists |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "1 graphic warning (hover for details)." | A [graphic](/graphics/overview/) warned while the file was drawn. | Each warning, with the graphic's name and its frame. |
| "1 cursor warning (hover for details)." | A clip's cursor file couldn't be drawn, so that clip is written without its pointer. | Each one, for example "The cursor of media 3 is not drawn: …" |

The cursor count comes after the graphic count. A finished row in the Export Queue shows the same counts, and its tooltip lists the same warnings.

## Failures

An export that can't run says why in a sentence, on the sheet or on its queue row. On the sheet, **Close** dismisses it.

| The sheet says | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| "There is nothing on the timeline to export — add a clip first." | Add a clip. |
| "The export was not started: the graphic …" | A graphic in the range doesn't compile or has no module. Fix it and export again. |
| "The export was stopped at frame … of the graphic …" | A graphic failed at that frame. No file is left. |
| "Clip … 's loudness or speech has not been measured yet…" | A clip's gate, leveller or de-esser can't be set. Wait for their Status rows to show the clip's loudness, then export again. |
| "Clip …'s retimed audio could not be rendered: …" | The sound of a speed change couldn't be made. |
| "Clip …'s isolated voice could not be rendered: …" | Voice Isolation couldn't be rendered for that clip. |
| "Clip …'s voice effect could not be rendered: …" | The voice effect couldn't be rendered for that clip. |
| "Clip …'s person masks could not be made: …" or "Clip …'s foreground masks could not be made: …" | A Remove Background clip's masks failed. No frame is written without them. |
| "This Mac cannot export with the “…” preset." | This Mac has no encoder for that format. Choose another format. No file is left. |
| "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…" | A custom size has a different shape from the canvas. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). |

Other messages come from macOS or the file being written, and appear as they are.

A failure is different from a cancel. A failed Animated GIF, Animated PNG or WebM export removes its partly written file, and so does a failed export with stems. Any other format that fails while writing can leave a partly written file at the path you chose. It isn't a finished export, so delete it.

## Quitting during an export

Quitting while the Exporting sheet is writing doesn't ask, and leaves the half-written file behind. Cancel the export first.

Only the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) is guarded at quit, so jobs there ask before they stop.

## With an agent

An agent's `export` puts a job on the Export Queue and answers at once, with no progress sheet. A bad argument, a missing folder, an empty timeline or a graphic that doesn't compile comes back from `export` before anything is queued. Failures while writing, the loudness figures and warnings come back from `export_status`, and `cancel_export` stops the job. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).

## Related

- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
- [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/)
- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)
- [Export loudness](/export/loudness/)

Where the code overrode the brief or guide:
- The Stems popup's first row is "None", not the scope's "No stems".
- Presets store Stems, Speed and Bit depth. Changing any of those three leaves the popup on the preset's name, and the page says so.
- A failed GIF, APNG or WebM export removes its file, as do failed stems, graphics and a missing encoder. Other formats can leave a partial file. The brief's code note only named graphics and stems.
- Cancelling on the sheet removes the destination even if it was an existing file you chose to replace. This is stated as a caution on export/progress-and-report.

Scope's "transparent presets": neither the guide nor the code has this as a feature. I covered what the code supports under Good to know on export/presets: the format is stored, nothing about the canvas, and a custom size of another shape can fail.

Left out of the docs, for the owner to look at: the comment on ProjectDocument.inOutRange says the export tool's handler must check scope and answer in a sentence, but AgentServer+Export.swift reads document.inOutRange with no scope check. An agent exporting range in_out inside a nest may therefore spend nest-local ticks as timeline time. I only read the code and did not run it, so the pages make no claim about an agent's in_out inside a nest.
